Bilawal says PTI hurting itself by not abandoning its 'extremist politics'
items.description: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari said on Friday that the PTI’s “extremist politics” were hurting the party itself, calling on it to reconsider its political strategy. “The PTI is a party that has public supporters, but it keeps disappointing the people because of its decisions and extremist politics,” Bilawal said while speaking to the media in Karachi. “It has no political role in this city or in the federal government, and if it continues this extremist politics, it will not remain in [power] in the province [Khyber Pakhtunkhwa] either.” The PTI has gone ahead with its march, aimed to demand the release of jailed party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan, despite warnings from the Centre, which has vowed to prevent any gatherings in Islamabad. “Instead of fulfilling their responsibilities and taking care of their province and its people, this party is stuck on the politics of hate,” Bilawal said. He added that a week earlier, the federal government and the entire system had been prepared to impose an emergency in KP. The PPP, he said, had consistently maintained that imposing an emergency or introducing governor’s rule was a constitutional and legal option, but one that should be treated as a “legal atom bomb” and used only as a last resort. In an apparent reference to talks between the government and opposition, he said, without explicitly naming anyone, that although all political parties including those in the opposition, had reached an agreement, the chief minister of one province had chosen “negative politics” instead of pursuing dialogue. He said that sometimes “extremist politics” were preferred when one was in opposition, but said that this was ultimately affecting “the country, that province and its people, the youth and most of all the PTI”. He called on the party to play its role in politics, adding that if it abandoned its current ways he would help to change the “political atmosphere” from Karachi itself. Bilawal said that Karachi had two political powers, the PPP and the PTI. However, the PTI is fighting with other political parties, the federal government, the judiciary, Parliament and the establishment. “When this is your politics, then your workers will also be disappointed,” he said. Bilawal said that the PTI had not participated in parliamentary proceedings. He said after several months, the PML-N had agreed to form a parliamentary committee on electoral reforms. “But it is expected that those crying the most about rigging … will not become a member of the committee. If you do not participate then how will we stop rigging in the future?” he asked. Bilawal said that the PPP, from one political party to another, was insisting to the PTI to abandon its “extremist politics”. He said that once that happened, the space for dialogue would open and the party would be able to address its concerns. “If they are true to their party and to their leader, if the chief minister who is so loud these days is true to Imran Khan, then he will abandon this extremist politics,” he said. “It is Pakistan’s history; if someone is in jail today, it does not mean they remain there tomorrow,” he said. Bilawal said his father, President Asif Ali Zardari held the “record” for being jailed the longest. “If PTI continues with its extremist politics, then Khan sahib will break Zardari sahib’s record and will remain a prisoner. If the PTI leaves its extremist politics, then it will be able to achieve its political goals and save its workers from becoming disillusioned. Let’s see if they listen to what I am saying,” he said. Bilawal said the country’s situation had deteriorated to the point where the public was facing hardships. “Poverty is increasing to such an extent that the World Bank is now saying that Pakistan is bearing the heaviest burden of poverty and unemployment in the entire region,” Bilawal said. “We want that whoever is the prime minister, in the federal government should be successful, so that the public gets relief. For creating those conditions, we need political stability, and this is only possible right now if political parties cooperate with each other on the country’s basic issues,” he said.

items.title: China urges Nigerian media to uphold one-China principle
items.description: The Chinese Embassy has urged Nigerian media organisations to distinguish between reporting on Taiwan and descriptions that could suggest the island is a sovereign country separate from China, prompting discussions on diplomatic sensitivities and editorial independence. Speaking at a meeting with media executives in Lagos, Mr Xu Fan, Director of Bilateral Relations and Commerce at the Chinese Consulate General in Lagos, said China’s position on Taiwan was rooted in historical records, international agreements and the diplomatic framework established after the Second World War. He cited United Nations General Assembly Resolution 2758 of 1971 and Nigeria’s diplomatic recognition of the People’s Republic of China, maintaining that the One-China Principle remained the political foundation of diplomatic relations between Beijing and Abuja. Xu noted that Nigeria reaffirmed its commitment to the principle during President Bola Tinubu’s state visit to China in September 2024. He clarified that China did not object to Nigerian media reporting on Taiwan but was concerned about terminology that could be interpreted as recognising the island as a sovereign state. The explanation prompted an exchange with Nigerian media executives, who stressed the importance of editorial independence and the freedom of journalists to report issues in the public interest. The meeting also examined Nigeria-China relations, trade, investment and media cooperation, highlighting the importance of dialogue between Chinese diplomatic institutions and Nigerian media organisations. The session was convened by Hon. Peter Ogbonna Eze, representative of Buffalo and Bay Media, and featured Ambassador Anderson Madubike, a former Nigerian High Commissioner to Australia, former Consul General in Shanghai, China, and former Chargé d’Affaires to South Africa. Earlier, Eze described Nigeria-China relations as a partnership that had expanded beyond traditional diplomatic engagement to encompass infrastructure, trade, education, technology, agriculture, investment and people-to-people exchanges. He urged media organisations to report the relationship accurately and in context, stressing that informed public discourse was essential to maximising the benefits of bilateral cooperation. “The media does not merely report events. It shapes how societies understand countries, people, policies and opportunities,” Eze said. Madubike, drawing on his diplomatic experience, described Nigeria-China relations as robust, citing extensive diplomatic, commercial and infrastructure ties between the two countries. He said the media had a critical role in sustaining diplomatic relations by shaping public perceptions, providing reliable information and promoting mutual understanding. “Diplomacy opens doors, but the media helps to keep those doors open,” he said. According to him, treaties and government agreements alone could not sustain long-term relationships between nations without public understanding and engagement. The diplomat stressed the importance of reporting the human dimension of Nigeria-China relations, including the experiences of Nigerian students, entrepreneurs and traders in China, as well as Chinese investors, engineers and business operators in Nigeria. He noted that credible information about markets, regulations, infrastructure, incentives and investment opportunities could encourage business partnerships and strengthen economic ties. The interaction also featured concerns about the trade imbalance between Nigeria and China, import dependence and complaints by Nigerian traders that some Chinese businesses were competing with them in the retail market. Responding, Xu acknowledged the concerns but argued that the solution should involve establishing clearer regulatory boundaries between wholesale and retail operations rather than excluding Chinese businesses from Nigeria. He said the Chinese Embassy had engaged Chinese traders, market authorities and other stakeholders to explore practical solutions. Xu also advocated a shift from a relationship dominated by trade in finished products towards greater Chinese investment in local manufacturing. He said Chinese companies could establish more factories and production facilities in Nigeria to create jobs, transfer skills and contribute to the country’s industrial development. The Chinese diplomat disclosed that bilateral trade reached approximately $28 billion in 2025, describing the figure as evidence of the growing economic relationship between both countries. He also said China had become Nigeria’s largest market for engineering contractors, its second-largest export market and China’s third-largest trading partner in Africa. Xu further highlighted China’s decision to extend zero-tariff treatment to 53 African countries with which it maintains diplomatic relations, including Nigeria. He said the policy presented opportunities for Nigerian agricultural products, including sesame, cashew nuts and cocoa, to gain greater access to the Chinese market, subject to applicable rules of origin, inspection and quarantine requirements. He urged Nigerian businesses to improve product quality, strengthen branding and take advantage of opportunities in the Chinese market. Illegal mining involving some Chinese nationals in Nigeria also featured prominently in the discussions. Xu distinguished between law-abiding Chinese businesses and individuals involved in illegal activities, insisting that violations of Nigerian law were unacceptable to the Chinese government and diplomatic authorities. He said the Chinese Embassy and relevant authorities were cooperating with Nigerian institutions by providing information and supporting efforts to identify Chinese nationals allegedly involved in illegal mining. According to him, the Chinese government would not shield individuals found to have violated Nigerian laws. Participants also called for deeper Chinese investment in manufacturing, technology transfer, industrial development and local value addition, arguing that bilateral cooperation should deliver greater benefits to Nigeria beyond infrastructure development and the importation of finished goods. The discussion highlighted the need for a partnership that promotes local production, employment, skills development and technological advancement. On media freedom, Nigerian executives reiterated that editorial independence remained a fundamental principle of journalism and that disagreements over sensitive diplomatic issues should be addressed through dialogue, clarification and the right of reply. In his concluding remarks, Xu described Nigerian media organisations as “partners and friends, not enemies.” He offered to strengthen cooperation with Nigerian media through professional exchanges, training programmes, seminars, media delegations and other institutional initiatives. He said Chinese authorities would continue to facilitate opportunities for Nigerian journalists to visit China, experience its development and gain a deeper understanding of its society, culture, economy and political system. Xu also invited participating media organisations to propose practical joint initiatives, including media programmes, publications and professional exchange projects. The engagement highlighted both the opportunities and challenges in Nigeria-China relations, particularly the need to reconcile diplomatic sensitivities with editorial independence and responsible journalism. Participants agreed that sustained dialogue, accurate reporting and stronger people-to-people engagement were essential to building mutual trust and ensuring that bilateral relations delivered greater benefits to both countries. The post China urges Nigerian media to uphold one-China principle appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La Côte d’Ivoire, entre ancrage occidental et diversification | Expliquez-moi…
items.description: La Côte d’Ivoire est aujourd’hui l’une des principales puissances économiques d’Afrique de l’Ouest. Hub commercial régional et premier producteur mondial de cacao, elle connaît une forte croissance. Pourtant, elle a connu des périodes de grande instabilité. Le « miracle ivoirien » des premières décennies d’indépendance s’essouffle dans les années 1980 avec la chute des cours des matières premières. Après la mort de Félix Houphouët-Boigny, son premier président au régime autoritaire, en 1993, des tensions politiques et identitaires émergent, jusqu’à plonger le pays dans la guerre civile en 2002, puis dans un nouveau conflit après la crise électorale de 2010-2011. Depuis, la Côte d’Ivoire a renoué avec une forte croissance et une relative stabilité. Sur le plan diplomatique, elle a reconstruit des liens étroits avec la France, après une décennie de distance sous la présidence de Laurent Gbagbo, tout en diversifiant progressivement ses partenariats, notamment avec la Chine. Les inégalités persistantes, les dérives autoritaires du régime d’Alassane Ouattara et le maintien de la menace terroriste à sa frontière nord conjuguée à de fortes tensions avec ses voisins sahéliens révèlent les limites d’une stabilité qui demeure fragile. Comment s’est construite la Côte d’Ivoire depuis la fin de la période coloniale ? Comment le « miracle ivoirien » a-t-il laissé place aux fractures et aux guerres civiles ? Et comment Abidjan cherche-t-elle aujourd’hui à s’affirmer entre ancrage occidental, diversification de ses partenariats et tensions régionales ? Retour en cartes, photos et infographies sur une puissance ouest-africaine au cœur des recompositions de la région. L’article La Côte d'Ivoire, entre ancrage occidental et diversification | Expliquez-moi… est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: La CAF porte son soutien annuel aux fédérations à 700.000 dollars
items.description: Le président de l'instance continentale, Patrice Motsepe, a annoncé que la Confédération africaine de football (CAF) a porté de 200.000 à 700.000 dollars le montant de son soutien financier annuel accordé aux associations membres. S'exprimant lors de la Conférence stratégique de la CAF, qui se tient du 7 au 9 octobre à Santa Maria, sur l'île de Sal au Cap Vert, en présence notamment du président de la Fédération internationale de football (FIFA), Gianni Infantino, Motsepe a précisé que cette augmentation avait été réalisée depuis 2021, soulignant l'engagement de l'instance continentale à renforcer les capacités financières des fédérations africaines. Le président de la CAF a également réaffirmé l'objectif de porter ce soutien à un million de dollars par association membre, grâce notamment au développement de partenariats commerciaux et à la mobilisation de nouveaux sponsors, notant que le Comité exécutif de la CAF devait examiner des offres d'entreprises présélectionnées en vue de nouer des partenariats destinés à accroître les ressources du football africain. Motsepe a, par ailleurs, insisté sur la nécessité d'investir davantage dans les académies, le football scolaire, les compétitions amateurs et les championnats professionnels. L'objectif à long terme était de permettre aux 54 associations membres de devenir financièrement autonomes, grâce à une coopération renforcée avec la FIFA, les gouvernements et le secteur privé. La Conférence stratégique de la CAF est consacrée notamment au développement du football africain, à l'amélioration de sa gouvernance et à la définition des priorités pour les prochaines échéances internationales. Le programme de ce vendredi comporte une session consacrée à l’analyse des performances africaines au Mondial 2026, avec la participation notamment du directeur du développement du football mondial de la FIFA, Arsène Wenger, et de plusieurs techniciens, dont le sélectionneur national, Mohamed Ouahbi. The post La CAF porte son soutien annuel aux fédérations à 700.000 dollars appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: « Deux poulets » : la demande poignante d’une future mariée algérienne
items.description: C’est une vidéo qui fait le buzz sur les réseaux sociaux. Une incroyable histoire qui prouve encore une fois, que les Algériennes et les Algériens ont un cœur grand comme l’océan et qu’ils sont toujours disposés à soutenir les personnes en difficulté. Partagée sur les réseaux sociaux, la vidéo est rapidement devenue virale, entraînant des réactions en chaîne. L’histoire se passe dans la wilaya de Ain Defla. A une future mariée, dont on n’aperçoit pas le visage et à qui l’on demande de quoi elle aurait besoin pour sa dot de mariage , celle-ci répond simplement : « Deux poulets pour le repas de mes noces ». Une réplique inattendue, qui a fait couler beaucoup d’encre et a eu un effet boule de neige. Une Algérienne demande juste deux poulets comme dot de mariage Elle n’a pas demandé la lune. Ni bijou, ni trousseau, ni méchoui, ni argent. Juste deux volatiles pour préparer le dîner de ses noces qui approche à grands pas et qu’elle n’a pas les moyens de financer. La future mariée s’est contentée de demander deux poulets. Cela a suffi par déclencher une vague de sympathie et de solidarité chez les internautes. Largement diffusée et relayée sur les réseaux sociaux, cette vidéo a fait le buzz. Le résultat ne s’est pas fait attendre. Bras chargés de cadeaux, des citoyens se sont précipités vers le domicile du futur couple. Même les enfants ont été mis à contribution, puisqu’on les voit transporter des présents avec leurs papas. Une belle leçon de générosité et de solidarité qui fait chaud au cœur. Salles des fêtes, trousseau, aide financière : l'incroyable chaîne de solidarité De toutes les régions du pays, ils ont afflué comme une armée pour apporter à la mariée une aide matérielle et lui offrir une fête inoubliable. Outre le trousseau destiné à lui procurer un peu de confort, une salle des fêtes a été louée et une cagnotte organisée. Et ce n’est pas tout : les généreux donateurs ont décidé d’octroyer à ce jeune couple sans ressources, une aide financière mensuelle. Une main tendue vers ces jeunes mariés qui démarrent leur vie conjugale avec très peu de moyens. La générosité et la solidarité des Algériens est légendaire. Cette capacité à se mobiliser pour les plus vulnérables ne date pas d’aujourd’hui. On a vu l’incroyable mobilisation lors des incendies du mois d’Août à Jijel ou lorsque Zahia, la jeune fille sous emprise de psychotropes a eu besoin d’aide pour suivre une cure de désintoxication. Cette entraide témoigne de valeurs humaines profondes, fondée sur l’empathie, la générosité et le sens du partage. L’article « Deux poulets » : la demande poignante d'une future mariée algérienne est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Kundi challenges PTI long march participants to cross Swabi
items.description: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi challenged PTI protesters on Friday to dare and cross Swabi, a Khyber Pakhtunkhwa district that borders Punjab’s Attock and which the opposition party in the Centre has announced as the eventual destination of its long march. The route plan for the march, being carried out to demand the release of jailed PTI founder Imran Khan, has undergone multiple changes since its launch on Oct 4. While the party initially vowed to march towards Islamabad, its final destination seemingly remains tentative as the KP CM has yet to announce the plan for the trek beyond Swabi. So far, the march has remained within KP, where the PTI is in power. The protesters were in Peshawar on Thursday and are expected to reach Charsadda today, as political temperatures between the PTI and the federal government remain high. As tensions remained high, Kundi raised doubt on the realisation on the PTI’s plan to reach Swabi on Oct 11. ““They are probably going to Charsadda today, then they might go to Mardan, and after that they might end up reaching Afghanistan through Dir,” he said while addressing a press conference in Peshawar. “Because whenever they turn towards Swabi, their legs start shaking, and their hearts tremble […] If they have any self-respect, reach Swabi tomorrow and cross it, or even step inside it. I will accept that you are a revolutionary party that aims to make a naya (new) Pakistan.” Continuing to rail against the party, he said senior PTI leaders were “sitting in drawing rooms” in Islamabad while others were in “hiding”. “They say that they have run successful mobilisation campaigns across Sindh and Punjab; did you see anyone from these provinces on their long march’s truck?” he questioned. Reacting to the PTI’s claims that KP lawmakers and cabinet members were being “abducted”, Kundi said: “You (KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi) should tell who is abducting your ministers as you are the chief executive of the province. “You cannot protect your ministers, MPAs, and MNAs; how will you protect my people, the province and the nation? This is your position.” Kundi added that the KP CM should and his cabinet to resign on “ethical grounds”. “They say that the SHOs do not listen to them; if no one listens to you, then why are you sitting [in the government]? Only to make money or for corruption,” he remarked, adding that presently, doctors, teachers, nurses, and municipal officers were observing strikes in KP. The KP governor vowed that “we will protect our province and fight against terrorism on the front line. We will show such incompetent people […] how a province is run.” Answering a question, Kundi contended that no province could run without the Centre. “But these people talk about confrontation with the federal government,” he said. On the possibility of governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, the governor said that when the president or the prime minister deem that the situation in the province had worsened to the extent that these options should be availed, they would make a decision. In response to another question, Kundi took a jibe at the PTI, saying the party had turned its long march into “Lucky Irani Circus, travelling from city to city […] But whenever they turn to Swabi, they opt to take a U-turn”. He also commented on his recent meeting with KP’s chief secretary and inspector general (IG) to discuss the province’s law and order situation. The KP CM has taken strong exception to the meeting and called for legislation to provide for the governor’s impeachment for “violating the Constitution”. Kundi defended the meeting, saying: “I called the chief secretary and IG because we have no government on the ground in the province; they are busy in their circus.” “My province is burning,” he continued, citing recent incidents of terrorism in KP. “They (PTI) have never condemned terrorism. They cannot challenge the terrorists […] They don’t have any plan to fight terrorism,” he claimed. He added that “terrorism is our red line,”, adding, “We cannot hand over this province to terrorists. This is our point agenda […] we will first talk on terrorism, and other things will follow.” The PTI march began after weekend talks with the federal government failed to bridge their differences for multiple reasons , particularly over the counterterrorism policy. The federal ministers are now also linking differences over the counterterrorism policy with the possibility of an emergency or governor’s rule in KP.

items.title: Mobilisation lycéenne en France : l’ONU met en garde contre un «recours disproportionné à la force»
items.description: « Nous suivons avec inquietude les incidents lies aux manifestations etudiantes et aux blocages de lycees en France, dont certains ont degenere en violences », a declare ce 9 octobre la porte-parole du Haut-Commissariat des Nations unies aux droits de l'homme (HCDH) Shabia Mantoo aux journalistes a Geneve, en reponse a une question de l'agence turque Anadolu. « Nous appelons chacun a veiller a ce que » les manifestations « restent pacifiques et a ce qu'il n'y ait pas de recours disproportionne a la force de la part des forces de l'ordre », a-t-elle souligne lors de ce point de presse, avant d'ajouter : « Le droit de reunion pacifique doit etre respecte. » En France, ou se deroule une nouvelle journee de mobilisation des lyceens, le ministere de la Justice a indique dans un communique que 6 877 personnes, dont 86 % de mineurs, ont ete placees en garde a vue depuis le debut de la contestation lyceenne mi-septembre a Creteil. Parmi elles, 2 376 font l'objet de poursuites, est-il precise. Vingt et un placements en detention provisoire ont ete ordonnes, concernant 15 majeurs et six mineurs, apprend-on egalement. Des centaines de blesses depuis le debut du mouvement Selon le syndicat policier UN1TE, au 7 octobre, 761 membres des forces de l'ordre ont ete blesses depuis le debut du mouvement. Deux jours plus tot, le ministre de l'education nationale edouard Geffray avait fait etat de 190 eleves blesses, avant d'evoquer un cas « personnellement et humainement dramatique » a propos du lyceen de 15 ans dont une main a ete arrachee lors d'une manifestation a Lens. « Attendre qu'un garcon de 15 ans ait la main arrachee pour suspendre l'usage de grenades assourdissantes, je trouve que c'est extremement inquietant », a estime ce 9 octobre sur franceinfo la secretaire generale de la Confederation francaise democratique du travail (CFDT) Marylise Leon, qui s'« interroge » sur le nombre d'interpellations. Toujours ce 9 octobre, edouard Geffray, sans donner le chiffre precis, a indique que « la journee d'hier nous a fait passer le cap des 100 personnels » de l'education nationale « blesses ». La veille au soir, de maniere tout aussi floue, le ministre avait annonce que 3 000 professeurs remplacants allaient etre reaffectes grâce a « un outil qu'on a dope a l'IA » dans les etablissements identifies comme prioritaires. « C'est edouard le magicien : hier ce n'etait pas possible et aujourd'hui on a 3 000 professeurs qui vont etre devant les etudiants », a fustige sur CNews le depute de Moselle et porte-parole du Rassemblement national Laurent Jacobelli, denoncant une « gestion par a-coups de la politique de l'education nationale » ainsi qu'une « legitimation de la violence » observee lors des manifestations lyceennes.

items.title: [Rediffusion] Say face au paludisme : prévention, sensibilisation et engagement communautaire
items.description: Listen to « Say face au paludisme : prevention, sensibilisation et engagement communautaire (Le forum) » on Spreaker. Le paludisme demeure l'un des principaux problemes de sante publique au Niger. Chaque annee, cette maladie touche de nombreuses personnes, en particulier les enfants de moins de cinq ans et les femmes enceintes, qui figurent parmi les populations les plus vulnerables. Le departement de Say n'est pas epargne. Les moustiques vecteurs du parasite responsable du paludisme y sont presents tout au long de l'annee, mais les cas de la maladie connaissent generalement une forte augmentation pendant la saison des pluies, periode particulierement favorable a la proliferation des moustiques. Malgre les efforts deployes, notamment la distribution de moustiquaires impregnees d'insecticide, les campagnes de sensibilisation et l'amelioration de la prise en charge des malades, le paludisme continue d'entraîner de nombreux cas de maladie et, parfois, des deces. La prevention constitue donc un moyen essentiel pour reduire les risques de transmission. Plusieurs gestes simples peuvent contribuer a proteger les populations : dormir regulierement sous une moustiquaire impregnee d'insecticide, maintenir son environnement propre, eliminer les eaux stagnantes qui servent de lieux de reproduction aux moustiques et se rendre rapidement dans un centre de sante des l'apparition de symptomes tels que la fievre. Mais la lutte contre le paludisme ne repose pas uniquement sur les mesures individuelles. La sensibilisation, l'engagement des communautes et la collaboration entre les populations, les autorites sanitaires et les differents partenaires jouent egalement un role determinant. C'est pourquoi, au cours de cette emission, nous tenterons de repondre a plusieurs questions : Quelle est l'importance de la sensibilisation dans la prevention du paludisme ? Comment renforcer l'engagement des communautes dans la lutte contre cette maladie ? Quel role les populations, les autorites sanitaires et les partenaires peuvent-ils jouer pour prevenir efficacement le paludisme et proteger la sante de tous ? Pour en debattre, nous avons invite : Salamatou ISSAKA, agente de sante ; Nouhou AMADOU, chef de quartier ; Laila ABOUBACAR, beneficiaire des produits distribues dans le cadre de la lutte contre le paludisme. Presentation : Fati Amadou. Photo par YASUYOSHI CHIBA / AFP

items.title: Métier : « Tiak Tiak » (Le billet de Omar DIOUF)
items.description: Ils étaient au début livreurs, ensuite ils sont devenus transporteurs de passagers. Le boom de la conduite de motos « Tiak Tiak » ou « Jakarta » connaît de jour en jour un regain si élevé que la circulation dans nos grandes villes est devenue infernale. Il est presque impossible pour les automobilistes de conduire sans avoir de bisbilles avec ces bonhommes pressés, slalomant insolemment avec leurs deux-roues. Ces activités précaires que nos jeunes gens de vingt à trente ans ne devraient exercer qu’un laps de temps sont devenues de véritables métiers pour ces hommes à la force encore vive, mais en manque de qualification professionnelle. Certains se transforment souvent en pickpockets ou agresseurs, l’occasion faisant le larron. Une insécurité grandissante dans les rues de Dakar et de sa grande banlieue ou même à Thiès, ville également gagnée par ces motos « Jakarta ». Comme ce fut avec les marchands ambulants, le phénomène des « Tiak Tiak » viendrait à dépasser des proportions non maitrisables par les autorités publiques. omar.diouf@lesoleil.sn

items.title: The Guardians
items.description: R aleigh stood in the morning sunlight under the big maple with a chainsaw in one hand and a heavy splitting maul in the other looking at his friend of 30 years. ’Course I got mix, he said. Next to the lawn-more in the back. Says mix on the side and don’t forget the bar and chain as well. Lawn mower , Silas said. It was an old joke between them. Raleigh was big and round-shouldered and had brown eyes that went flat and unseeing when he was thinking about something else. I’m a librarian trapped in a prizefighter’s body, he liked to say. An out-of-shape prizefighter. Silas came back with fuel mix and bar and chain oil and his maul. He was 60 but moved with the precision of an athlete and checked the corners of every room he walked into as if he always expected something to happen. Why the fuck are you always looking around? Raleigh demanded once at breakfast, but Sally shushed him. She had a soft spot for Silas as if he were her wayward son. Well, he looks like a sociopath, Raleigh said. All the tools went into the back of the truck along with the old cutting chaps with the gash across the right leg where the Kevlar had saved his knee joint 20 years ago. The bed was still matted with dead leaves from the previous fall. Silas grabbed the door gutter and swung himself into the passenger seat and Raleigh climbed in on the driver’s side and started the truck and found the old ruts that skirted the overgrown fields. Silas had visited Raleigh out here through girlfriends and deaths and illnesses and presidents and wars, but now everything suddenly seemed like a very long time ago. The house faced west toward a semicircle of mountains with meadows stretching up their flanks past stone walls that ran into the woods, the lower maples and oaks still in their colors but the upper ridges dead-brown and ready for winter. When they were young men, Silas and Raleigh had climbed to the top of the ridge, passing through the fallen stone walls and the sugar maples and then the dark groves of red pines and finally to the views—west toward the ridges and mean little towns of the Delaware headwaters and east toward the prettier country and bigger farms of the Schoharie. They’d built a fire and gotten drunk talking about how their lives were going to go and had woken up just before dawn with the fire dead and big aimless snowflakes sifting through the treetops. He and Raleigh had started stiffly down the mountain, still drunk and their plans gone. The girls good? Little one’s just starting to read, and Sarah’s in third grade and doing fifth-grade math, Silas said. They affected by what’s going on? Of course, Silas said. Raleigh waited for more, and eventually Silas went on, Mostly they’re worried about their friends and their plans and everything. They’re little girls. They’ve already got more friends than I had in my whole life. Raleigh and Sally never had kids, because they couldn’t, and sometimes Silas could almost feel those unrealized children flitting overhead to remind everyone of the little triumphs and sorrows that had never happened. Of the love that had never found anywhere to go. The whole point is just for them to grow and break your heart, Silas eventually said. That’s what no one realizes until it’s too late. Every time Raleigh hit a bump the chainsaws leaped from the bed and came back down, and Silas would say, Fuck, Rawls. Raleigh guided the truck uphill through the high field and stopped by a dead ash the color of bone that loomed out of the woods. They got out and laid the saws on the open tailgate without speaking and gassed them and oiled them and re-tensioned the chains. They never spoke while they worked unless they needed to. Silas choked the big Stihl and pull-started it and got it running and engaged the chain brake with the heel of his hand and then set it on the ground, where it sat shaking eagerly. He clapped on his earpro and waded through the overgrown field to the ash and cleared a work area for himself—a way to get out if things went wrong. There were a few rocks underfoot that he pitched into the woods and then he faced the tree with his feet apart like a boxer. A chainsaw made him slow and methodical in a way that nothing else ever had. Raleigh never complimented Silas, because they knew each other too well for that, but he enjoyed watching him work. The calculation and lack of urgency until everything tipped. Silas made the top and bottom cuts and kicked the wedge out and ringed the backside of the tree to mark his level. It was dense wood, dead and very hard, and the trunk was at least two feet across, big enough to bury the big saw. When a tree goes, you see it first by the tiniest widening of the kerf, a slight offset to the angle. You don’t see it in the canopy. With the tree balanced on the last bit of holding wood Silas felt young again, as if the entire world were waiting for him to make his move. He re-slotted the saw bar into the kerf and revved the saw and touched the cut, which was all it took, and then switched off the saw and backed up with his eyes on the canopy. Death comes from above, his father always said. The big tree creaked and objected and slowly, heavily started dropping with the backcut gaping open in a kind of shock and a full 10 tons of wood crashing sickly to Earth after a hundred years of defiance. The sound rolled through the woods and then the forest was quiet for a few moments as if paying respects to its dead. Silas propped the saw bar on the toe of his boot and palmed the handle so that it stayed balanced, and the two men stood in the new gash of sunlight. Dust rose and swirled where the tree had once been. Silas’s father had been a logger in Montana and put himself through college setting wire chokers on mountainsides in the Absarokas, and Silas was now 10 years older than his dad had ever been—cancer, dead in three months. His mom and dad were divorced by then but she was still with him at the very end, and she never recovered. Silas was overseas at the time and stayed there, and his mother was gone a couple of years after that. A cord, minimum, he said, maybe more, but you’ll have to split all that big stuff. It’ll be a lot of work. Raleigh walked past Silas out of the weeds and brambles and pull-started the small saw. He began limbing out the crown while Silas worked the other end with the Stihl, cutting clean rounds that thudded into the weeds. The biggest part of the trunk hung off the edge of a drainage ditch, so he didn’t have to do an undercut or worry about dulling his chain. After half an hour he and Raleigh stopped to drink water out of a big mason jar in the truck and then sat on what remained of the trunk like elephant hunters of an earlier era. Silas lit a cigarette and they sat without talking and Silas smoked and then crushed the butt out on the dead tree. I’ve always loved those things, he said, jutting his chin at the fieldstone cairns in the field. I put those up almost 20 years ago now, Raleigh said. I know that. There were four cairns, taller than a man and weirdly animated for piles of rocks; if you looked away and then back again, you could almost think they’d moved. They stretched across the top of the meadow 50 yards apart, looking east past the house. Raleigh called them the Guardians, and Silas pictured his friend shirtless and bent on a July day lugging huge stones through the field grass, half mad and slick with sweat. It had been a tough time for Raleigh back then, Silas knew. When he and Sally had finally given up, he went inward and she went outward, he liked to say, but their hearts stayed in the same place. This property, man, Silas said, shaking his head. How much are you up here? Pretty much full-time since I retired, Raleigh said. Sally’s in the city most of the time—her friends, her volunteer work. What do you do when you’re up here? I don’t know, he said. This. You ever get lonely? Not in the way you mean, Raleigh said. What way is that? Raleigh thought for a moment. Hollow, he finally said. Like there’s nothing inside you to keep you up. The Guardians cast their stone gaze down the valley, their shadows swept behind them as if into a headwind and the October morning hot enough for insects and heat to rise off the fields. The house was set prettily at the mouth of the valley, an old post-and-beam with most of the original angles and roofline gone and a sunroom and deck now facing the wide embrace of the hills. Silas had had children late in life—very late—and now his sole concern was to see his girls into adulthood. How do you tell an 8-year-old that much of her father’s life was just a series of impulsive swerves that deprived her of having a father for as long as little girls should? After Silas finished his cigarette, he stood up and pull-started the saw. He worked his way up the trunk, cutting 14-inch lengths to fit into Raleigh’s woodstoves, wedging the top of the cuts with a maul or a piece of wood to keep them from binding the saw. When he was done, he stood and looked around at the carnage and walked the big saw over to the truck and grabbed the maul. He moved slowly through the exploded tree, splitting the rounds into quarters or sixths. Raleigh did the same, and their maul-swings thocked off the treeline and past the Guardians and across the meadow without rhythm or urgency. The two men worked silently for an hour, and then Raleigh tossed his maul over to the truck. I’m done, he said. It would have been a good day’s work at half their age. They filled the bed with split wood and piled the tools on top and climbed in. I don’t ever remember an October that felt like midsummer, Raleigh said. I don’t remember a fall that didn’t come with at least a good freeze and a little snow. Silas didn’t like talking about the changing climate, because it frightened him. Everything frightened him lately, which was strange because when he was young, almost nothing had. He’d just feel himself go empty until nothing mattered. Once, he’d spent an afternoon waiting to be shot by teenagers at a checkpoint that had bodies scattered all around it but in the end, they just returned his windbreaker and cigarettes and told him to be on his way. That was in West Africa, where most of the really bad stuff had happened, but even that hadn’t affected him much. Just some bad dreams and a strange new hot temper that felt surprisingly good when it showed up. Raleigh took a different route home that crossed the fields below the Guardians and dropped into a streambed—now dried to a trickle in the drought—and climbed the far embankment. There was flood wrack caught up in the timber and bittersweet thickets, and Silas commented that the creek must be quite a sight when she was running high. If you fell in, you’d get flushed straight to the bottom of the valley, Raleigh said. He stopped the truck in front of the woodpile and they walked the saws and mix into the garage and left the wood and the mauls for later. The house was cool and calm with skylights and handsome oak floors. The kitchen open in the modern style and centered around a hardwood island with a set of copper pans above it. A cream-colored cast-iron stove waited for winter in the sunroom. Silas pictured two feet of snow piled against the floor-to-ceiling windows and the field and ridges quilted and muffled and white in the distance. Raleigh came back from the kitchen with two cans of beer, and they sat on the nice furniture, sawdust still plastered to their skin, and took a few sips. That was good work, Silas eventually said. Good hard work. How are things in New York? You and Helen okay? No, but we will be. You think there’s any chance of reconciling? None. Sally talked to her the other day. I know she did. It seems like she misses you. I miss her too. What are you going to do? You’re lookin’ at it, Silas said. Raleigh tipped his beer back and swallowed and brought it back down. You ever thought about going back overseas? Wouldn’t do it for any price at all. Like literally, there isn’t a number. Seems like it would be easy. It would be. Is it the girls? Partly, but I also don’t want to get killed doing something that won’t make any difference. The world’s just gonna keep doing whatever the world’s gonna keep doing. What about the time they were going to shoot that guy, Raleigh said. And you— He didn’t finish, because Silas was looking out the window, and Raleigh knew him well enough to know he was now watching shrouds of monsoon rain coming off the ocean and thundering across the zinc roofs and ropes of water twisting through the red clay streets and young fighters, children, in the backs of pickup trucks soaking wet with their guns and their useless ponchos. Or something very much like that. After a while, Silas cleared his head with a shake and looked back at Raleigh. I saw a man bring his little boy into a clinic, Silas said. Raleigh didn’t say anything, because he knew he didn’t have to. Way up in the north in the highlands, it wasn’t even during the war but it might as well have been. The boy had malaria and his dad was carrying him in his arms and running as fast as he could. The boy was shaking and had these big bright eyes that were already sort of looking off at the next world … Even I could tell he wasn’t going to make it. And the dad was just frantic. He laid his boy down on a cot and the rain was hammering all around us and the generator was out so there was nothing but kerosene lamps. Raleigh took a drink, and something unwelcome flicked across his face—a tug at the corner of his mouth, a quick blink. The doctor just gave the kid aspirin because there weren’t even enough antibiotics for the people who had a chance, and the father saw that. The father knew. And the boy swallowed the pill and asked if he was going to heaven and the dad said, No, you’re staying right here with me. But he was crying when he said it and the boy knew as well. He’d stopped shaking for some reason and his eyes were very bright and he took his daddy’s hand and just— Silas stopped speaking because he couldn’t anymore and tried again after a few moments but still couldn’t and so he gave up, and the two men just sat avoiding each other’s eyes and watching the day stretch out and lie down outside. I t was almost dark , and Silas spoke quietly into the receiver of the wall phone because Raleigh was asleep in the next room. Hi, Helen. He waited through the silence and then said, I’m just calling to check on the girls. They’re fine, Silas. Would you like to talk to them? That’s okay. Silas, why are you calling? He didn’t know what to say. Because I miss you, he finally said. I miss you too. I’m up at Raleigh’s and it just made me think of you. Helen didn’t answer. It just made me think maybe we could still all come up here together like we used to. That’s not a good idea, she said. You know that. Silas looked through the plate-glass doors at the failing day. Helen, you have no idea how sorry I am. I know you are, Silas. But here we are now and it’s okay. S ilas took his cigarettes out to the deck and sat down in an Adirondack chair. The sun’s last effort lay raftered in red and gold across the peaks and the valley was already in darkness. He shook a cigarette from the pack and lit it and inhaled and leaned back and slowly let the smoke out. He didn’t smoke at home and he didn’t smoke for months at a time but when he smoked, he smoked. A chevron of wake spread across the pond and died out before reaching the shore, a beaver at her last tasks. Silas smoked and watched her in the collapsing light. His eyes finally wandered up-valley to the Guardians and then back again, and that was when he noticed it: a slight movement. A shift in things. He pulled his glasses out of his shirt pocket and rubbed them with his sleeve and put them on. He checked the pond again, now suddenly in focus, and then stabbed his vision back up the valley. The Guardians were motionless while he looked at them but moved when he looked away—just enough to get somewhere without getting caught. Silas shook his head and smiled like he was in on a joke but after a while realized he wasn’t in on shit. The great stones kept their resolute formation across the field but steadily, heavily were headed toward the house. Silas tried to tell himself he was just playing with the idea, but fear trickled thinly from his guts into the tops of his thighs. The woods were beautiful, and he’d never really stopped to think about that; the whole weekend he hadn’t stopped to think about it once. He looked back at the Guardians with their blunt faces and wondered whether he should keep staring so they’d have to stay put. Eventually he’d have to look away, though, and that’s when they’d move. The stones have all the time in the world, Silas thought. They’ve got so much time, they don’t even know what time is. Silas stubbed out his cigarette and turned his attention to the beaver. She was still working. Should he wake Raleigh up, he wondered, or just let him sleep? Would he want to see this? The Guardians would be in his house by dinner. What will it be like when they arrive? Silas wondered. What will happen when all their houses are filled with stone?

items.title: Carte biométrique : AODI veut simplifier le parcours des patients
items.description: © Internet Se faire soigner commence souvent par une longue attente. Dossiers papier, files interminables et informations médicales dispersées compliquent le parcours des patients. La startup malienne AODI propose une réponse numérique fondée sur une carte biométrique de santé. Il est 7 heures lorsque Fadiga franchit les portes d’un hôpital de Bamako, poussée par de violentes douleurs abdominales. Elle n’en ressort qu’à 20 heures. « Entre-temps, je me tordais de douleur et je pleurais », confie-t-elle. Autour d’elle, les patients affluent et l’attente se prolonge. Cette scène illustre les difficultés d’un système de santé encore faiblement numérisé. Le dossier papier reste courant et peut compliquer le suivi des malades entre plusieurs structures. Publié en 2023 dans le cadre du projet SanDi, un rapport de chercheurs de l’Université de Sherbrooke relève aussi les limites du cadre juridique malien concernant la vie privée, la collecte et la sécurité des données médicales. Innovation C’est en observant des situations comme celle de Fadiga qu’AODI, fondée par Astou Oumar Diallo, a conçu son premier projet. La carte donnerait accès, grâce à un identifiant biométrique et à la technologie NFC, à un dossier médical numérique regroupant antécédents, allergies, résultats d’examens et observations des soignants. Présentée devant un lecteur compatible, elle permettrait d’identifier rapidement le patient et de retrouver ses informations. Elle ne suffit toutefois pas, à elle seule, à assurer une consultation à distance. Chaque utilisateur disposerait d’un identifiant de santé personnel et portable. Le dispositif pourrait simplifier la vérification des droits des assurés et éviter la reconstitution du dossier à chaque passage. Il ne supprimerait pas toutes les files d’attente, mais réduirait le temps consacré à l’identification et à la recherche des informations. L’ensemble serait piloté par un logiciel également nommé AODI. Chaque hôpital ou Centre de santé communautaire disposerait d’un accès distinct. La startup annonce des serveurs sécurisés et des partenariats techniques, mais plusieurs garanties devront être précisées : lieu d’hébergement, chiffrement, sauvegarde, traçabilité des consultations, consentement du patient et règles de partage des données. De simples identifiants et mots de passe ne suffisent pas à préserver le secret médical. Pour des patients comme Fadiga, chaque heure perdue compte. La carte ouvre une piste pour fluidifier le parcours de soins, mais son utilité devra être démontrée par des essais en conditions réelles, l’adhésion des structures sanitaires et une protection rigoureuse des données sensibles. Ibrahim Baby

items.title: Chopmoney Bookkeeping seeks to simplify bookkeeping for Ghana’s small businesses
items.description: Chopmoney, a digital bookkeeping application, is seeking to help small businesses in Ghana improve their record-keeping by making it easier to track sales, expenses, and customer debts on their mobile phones. The application offers an alternative to handwritten records, allowing business owners to record daily transactions and generate invoices without having to work through complicated accounting processes. For a provision shop owner or market trader, keeping proper records can be difficult when serving customers, buying stock and attending to suppliers all fall on the same person. Some transactions are written down immediately. Others are left until the close of business, when the owner must rely on memory to put the figures together. The challenge becomes more pronounced when customers buy on credit or make part-payment. A business may be making sales, but without an accurate record of expenses and unpaid balances, the owner may struggle to determine how much money is available to keep it running. Chopmoney is designed to bring these records together, giving owners a clearer picture of their day-to-day business finances. Rather than searching through several pages of a notebook, users can record a sale, enter an expense or check a customer’s outstanding balance through the application. Its invoicing feature also allows businesses to provide customers with a clear record of amounts due. For businesses that regularly sell on credit, keeping track of repayments is particularly important. An owner needs to know not only who owes the business, but also how much has been paid and what remains outstanding. Keeping those records up to date can make follow-ups more straightforward and reduce disagreements arising from incomplete entries or forgotten payments. Beyond collecting debts, proper bookkeeping helps business owners assess whether sales are covering the cost of running the enterprise. Money received during the day may still be needed to replace stock, pay suppliers or meet transport and other operating expenses. Having these details available can support decisions on restocking, managing costs and setting money aside for upcoming payments. The application also uses artificial intelligence (AI) to analyse business performance and explain the results in plain language. Its AI business summary helps owners understand how the business has performed compared with previous periods. The aim is to make the figures useful to owners who may not have accounting training. Rather than looking at totals alone, they can use the explanations to understand changes in sales and spending, and consider how outstanding customer payments are affecting the business. The importance of record-keeping also extends to access to finance. In a report published by MyJoyOnline on October 6 , GCB Bank’s Head of Micro and Small Enterprises, Cedric McAddy, identified poor record-keeping and inadequate documentation as challenges facing businesses seeking funding from financial institutions. Consistent business records can help owners explain their financial position when seeking support, although access to credit remains subject to each lender’s requirements. For Chopmoney, the focus is on making the basic task of keeping those records more manageable. A business owner does not have to wait until the end of the week to begin putting sales and expenses in order. Transactions can be recorded as they occur and reviewed as part of the daily routine. The usefulness of the application will, however, depend on how consistently it is used. Missing sales, unrecorded expenses and outdated customer balances will still leave gaps, whether the records are kept in a notebook or on a phone. For small businesses looking to move from handwritten accounts to digital records, Chopmoney offers a practical starting point. Its value lies in helping owners keep track of the money coming into the business, the money going out and the payments yet to be received. Business owners can find out more at www.mychopmoney.com or download ChopMoney: Bookkeeping & Sales on the Google Play Store for Android devices.

items.title: Barcelona estrena el ‘decreto Maricarmen’ con una subida del IBI hasta el 150% a los pisos turísticos
items.description: Solo dos días después de la aprobación de los decretos sobre vivienda del Gobierno en el Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE) , el Ayuntamiento de Barcelona ha aprobado este viernes en comisión un recargo en el Impuesto de Bines Inmuebles (IBI) de los apartamentos turísticos de entre el 50% y el 150%. items.title: Scandale immobilier en Côte d’Ivoire : : Les aveux et explications de Serey Dié face aux victimes de Maman Caï-Caï
items.description: L'onde de choc de l'affaire « Maman Caï-Caï », portant sur une escroquerie immobilière présumée de plus de 320 millions de FCFA attribuée à Rita Bénédicte Djédjé Grahon et sa société Ivoire Challenge Corporation SARL, continue de secouer le monde des médias et des réseaux sociaux. Alors que la justice a placé la promotrice sous mandat de dépôt, plusieurs figures publiques réagissent pour désamorcer les soupçons de complicité. C'est le cas de l'ancien capitaine des Éléphants, Geoffroy Serey Dié, qui a publiquement rompu le silence pour expliquer avoir simplement voulu soutenir une entrepreneuse locale, révélant malgré lui les rouages d'une stratégie de communication reposant sur le prestige des célébrités. Dans l'immense scandale foncier qui éclabousse la société Ivoire Challenge Corporation SARL et sa promotrice Rita Bénédicte Djédjé Grahon (surnommée Maman Caï-Caï), l'heure des explications a sonné pour les personnalités publiques dont les visages avaient servi de caution morale auprès des souscripteurs. Face aux vives réactions des victimes et aux poursuites engagées par le Pôle Pénal Économique et Financier, l'ancien capitaine de la sélection nationale de football, Geoffroy Serey Dié , a pris la parole dans une vidéo clarificatrice pour rejeter toute implication dans les manœuvres frauduleuses. Dans son intervention diffusée sur les réseaux sociaux, Serey Dié tient à rétablir sa version des faits quant à ses apparitions aux côtés de Rita Djédjé. L'ex-international ivoirien explique avoir perçu la promotrice comme une compatriote courageuse cherchant à entreprendre dans l'immobilier. « Quand on voit des personnes sur internet qui essaient de se débattre […], on a envie de leur donner de la force » , plaide-t-il, précisant n'avoir agi que dans un esprit de solidarité et d'encouragement, motivé notamment par la présence de la comédienne Maman Adrienne (Adrienne Koutouan). L'ancien footballeur affirme catégoriquement n'avoir entretenu aucun lien commercial ni personnel durable avec la femme d'affaires. Il indique n'avoir eu aucun contact préalable ni ultérieur avec elle en dehors de cette séquence et rejette toute idée d'avoir perçu des contreparties pour induire les Ivoiriens en erreur ou leur vendre du rêve. Cette prise de parole met en lumière la mécanique centrale du réseau mis en cause : coller l'image de la société à des figures respectées ou très populaires pour inspirer confiance aux épargnants. En s’affichant avec des figures du sport, du cinéma ou du Web (comme Adrienne Koutouan, Serey Dié ou Yakyaka de Paris), la promotrice est parvenue à bâtir une illusion d'inviolabilité et de sérieux. Comme le soulignent plusieurs observateurs et analystes du Web, cette stratégie d'adossement d'image visait à crédibiliser des ventes de terrains dont l'entreprise ne possédait pas les titres de propriété légaux. Si certains acteurs comme Yakyaka de Paris ont brandi leurs contrats et invité ouvertement les victimes à porter plainte devant la justice, la pression s'accentue sur l'ensemble des personnalités citées pour qu'elles clarifient leurs relations financières avec Ivoire Challenge Corporation. Au-delà du cas personnel de Serey Dié, ce scandale repose la question de la responsabilité des créateurs de contenu et des célébrités dans le cadre d'appels publics à l'épargne ou de campagnes promotionnelles. Alors que la justice poursuit ses investigations et que la promotrice demeure sous les verrous, la Toile ivoirienne exige désormais une transparence totale de la part de tous les influenceurs impliqués. Pour les observateurs, toute abstention de s'expliquer publiquement ou de présenter des justificatifs contractuels risque d'être interprétée comme un aveu de complicité dans l'extorsion des 320 millions de FCFA soutirés aux souscripteurs. L’article Scandale immobilier en Côte d'Ivoire : : Les aveux et explications de Serey Dié face aux victimes de Maman Caï-Caï est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Avis d'Appel d'offres pour le recrutement d'un prestataire, expert du domaine des systèmes d'informations géographiques (SIG), pour réalisation de la cartographie des différentes réalisations du projet Ngourdam Pro-ARIDES
items.description: N°05-2026-SNV-Projet Ngourdam Pro-ARIDES Au Burkina Faso, SNV accompagne depuis plusieurs décennies les acteurs publics, communautaires et privés dans la mise en œuvre de solutions durables favorisant la résilience des populations vulnérables, notamment les ménages pastoraux et agropastoraux. Dans le cadre du Programme RESILIA financé par la Coopération Suisse (DDC), SNV met en œuvre le projet Ngourdam Pro-ARIDES sur une période de 45 mois (Décembre 2025 – Août 2029), qui vise à renforcer la résilience des communautés pastorales et agropastorales face aux crises climatiques, économiques et sécuritaires. Ce projet intervient dans 20 communes relevant de quatre (04) régions à savoir la région du Nando (dans les communes de Nanoro, Imasgho, Dalo, Gao, To, Bieha, Boura et Léo), dans la région du Nazinon (dans les communes de Béré, Bindé, Gogo, Guiaro et Manga), dans la région du Djôro (dans la commune de Djigouè, Gaoua, Kampti et Ouessa) et dans la région du Tannouyan (dans les communes de Banfora, Niangoloko et Soubakaniédougou). Le projet prévoit la réalisation d'une diversité d'ouvrages agropastoraux dans les différentes communes d'intervention. Pour toutes ces infrastructures, il est prévu la réalisation de cartes pour permettre de mieux les visualiser. C'est à cet effet que SNV entend s'attacher les services d'un cabinet ou d'un consultant spécialisé dans la réalisation des cartes à l'aide des systèmes d'informations géographiques (outils SIG) d'où le présent appel à candidature. C'est pourquoi, SNV au Burkina Faso, invite par le présent, les cabinets ou consultants individuels intéressés par le présent avis, à présenter des offres. Les termes de références peuvent être téléchargés dans le lien suivant : https://urlz.fr/vjvJ Les offres techniques et financières établies en langue française doivent être déposées sous pli fermé au plus tard le lundi 19 octobre 2026 au plus tard à 10heures 00 minutes TU au secrétariat de la SNV sis à Ouaga 2000 Sect. 54, 264 Av. Gérard Kango OUEDRAOGO Porte 287 ; 01 BP : 625 Ouagadougou 01, Burkina Faso La mention sur le pli fermé doit être « Sélection d'un.e Consultant.e, expert.e SIG au profit du Projet Ngourdam Pro ARIDES ». Le pli doit contenir également une clé USB contenant l'offre financière et l'offre technique intégralement scannées en version pdf. Pour tous renseignements, veuillez envoyer un email à bguiro@snv.org en mettant en copie syonli@snv.org SNV Burkina Faso se réserve le droit de ne donner aucune suite à tout ou une partie du présent appel d'offres. Pour ce faire, les soumissionnaires en seront informés. Ouagadougou, le 08/10/2026 Le Directeur Pays de SNV au Burkina Faso

items.title: Bamako Fashion Week 2026 : le patrimoine textile à l’honneur
items.description: © Internet La 3e édition de la Bamako Fashion Week se tiendra du 8 au 10 octobre 2026 au Mémorial Modibo Keïta, à Bamako. Placée sous le thème « La mode, levier de développement économique, social, culturel et environnemental », elle mettra particulièrement en valeur la création et le patrimoine textile africain. L’événement signe le retour de ce rendez-vous, plus de onze ans après la première édition organisée en février 2015 en hommage à Chris Seydou. Le styliste malien demeure une référence pour avoir introduit le bogolan dans la haute couture et contribué à son rayonnement international. Coorganisée par Mariam Bocoum et Makhossi, avec l’appui technique de Mali Mode Association, la manifestation veut replacer les matières et les savoir-faire maliens au centre de la création contemporaine. Bogolan, coton tissé, teintures et cuirs locaux devraient y côtoyer des formes et des coupes nouvelles, dans un dialogue entre héritage et modernité. Pour Mariam Bocoum, coorganisatrice, la Fashion Week doit aussi révéler la diversité des expressions vestimentaires maliennes et offrir une visibilité aux nouvelles générations de créateurs. « Le Mali regorge de talents », souligne-t-elle, en insistant sur la nécessité de mieux faire connaître leurs créations. Le rendez-vous leur donnera l’occasion de proposer leur propre lecture des formes, des couleurs et des symboles locaux. Programme chargé Des panels, un Forum de la mode et des masterclasses sont prévus. Ces rencontres permettront aux stylistes, artisans, tisserands, teinturiers et jeunes créateurs d’échanger sur les techniques, la transmission des savoirs et les nouvelles manières d’interpréter les étoffes africaines. Elles doivent aussi rapprocher les différents métiers qui participent à l’identité visuelle de la mode malienne. Pendant trois jours, Bamako accueillera des créateurs, des médias et des invités du Sénégal, du Burkina Faso, du Niger, de Côte d’Ivoire et de la diaspora. Le programme prévoit une cérémonie d’ouverture accompagnée d’un défilé collectif, un espace réservé aux talents émergents, un Défilé du Sahel, un Défilé Nouvelle Génération et un Défilé international. Des rencontres professionnelles et des espaces de cocréation compléteront ces présentations. Elle entend ainsi « transformer nos savoir-faire en produits contemporains », affirme Mariam Bocoum. Cette 3e édition veut présenter la mode comme une expression culturelle à part entière. Elle entend favoriser la transmission entre générations, faire connaître les techniques locales et montrer comment les créateurs maliens renouvellent leur patrimoine sans en effacer les références. Ali Sankaré

items.title: Beyond word of mouth: Bizella’s bid to build trust in Ghana’s services market
items.description: Digital services marketplace Bizella is seeking to make it easier for customers in Ghana to find vetted professionals for home repairs and personal care, while helping local service providers reach more clients. The platform allows users to compare providers, book appointments, and make payments through a mobile app. Its services include plumbing, electrical work, air-conditioning repairs, cleaning, painting, carpentry, and beauty and hair care. Available on Android and iOS, Bizella’s website currently highlights service coverage across Greater Accra. The company’s proposition addresses a familiar concern for households and businesses: finding someone who can be trusted to do the job properly. When a pipe bursts or an electrical fault develops, recommendations from friends, neighbours and colleagues can provide a useful starting point. But when those contacts are unavailable, customers may have limited information about the professionals they are considering. Bizella is positioning itself as a way to make that decision more informed, bringing provider information, bookings and payment management into one place. “Our founders experienced this problem firsthand and set out to build a platform where customers get peace of mind, and providers get the respect and income they deserve,” the company says on its About Us page . Verification and payment protection According to the company, professionals undergo a multi-step verification process before taking their first job on the platform. This covers identity, references, work history and trade certification where available, as well as professionalism standards. Customers can review profiles, photographs of previous work and customer ratings before choosing a provider. They can also check availability and select a booking time. The aim is to give customers more than a name and a phone number when deciding whom to hire. Bizella says a provider’s price is displayed before a booking is confirmed. Customers can then pay through the app using mobile money or a bank card. The company’s payment arrangement, Bizella Safepay, allows customers to pay upfront while their funds are held until they confirm that the work has been completed to their satisfaction. This means making a payment is separate from releasing the money to the service provider. The arrangement is intended to reduce the uncertainty associated with paying before a job has been delivered. For customers who are dissatisfied, Bizella says its support team should be contacted within 24 to 48 hours. The company states that payment remains on hold while the issue is addressed, with a resolution potentially including having the service carried out again. Verification and payment protection are useful, but the quality of the customer experience will still depend on providers delivering the agreed work and the platform responding effectively when problems arise. A wider market for local professionals For service providers, Bizella offers another route to customers beyond personal recommendations and existing contacts. A plumber, carpenter, cleaner, or beauty professional can use a digital profile to showcase previous work and make their services visible to people looking to hire. The platform also offers tools for managing availability, handling bookings and receiving digital payments. For skilled professionals whose businesses depend heavily on referrals, the opportunity is to reach customers outside their immediate networks. Someone seeking a service can assess their work without needing a mutual contact to make an introduction. Customer reviews can also help providers build a visible record of their performance. Over time, that record can support a professional reputation that extends beyond individual recommendations. Bizella’s promise will be tested beyond the booking screen: in professionals arriving as agreed, customers receiving the service they paid for, and complaints being resolved fairly. That is where a digital marketplace earns the trust that word of mouth has traditionally provided. Bizella is available on the Google Play Store and Apple App Store . Further information is available at bizella.com .

items.title: Bangladesh to replace Pakistan in Asian Hockey Champions Trophy
items.description: Bangladesh have accepted an invitation from the Asian Hockey Federation (AHF) to replace Pakistan in the Men’s Asian Hockey Champions Trophy 2026, scheduled to be held in India from October 27 to November 5. The AHF on Friday announced the revised schedule for the tournament without Pakistan following the country’s decision to withdraw from the event after its request for a neutral venue was rejected. The Pakistan Hockey Federation (PHF) had formally approached the continental body, seeking either the relocation of the entire tournament or the staging of Pakistan’s matches at a neutral venue, citing the sensitive bilateral situation between Pakistan and India and concerns over the safety and dignity of players and officials. Hockey India and the AHF turned down the proposal, insisting that the tournament would be held as scheduled at the designated venues in Jalandhar and Mohali. Following the decision, the PHF informed the AHF that Pakistan would not travel to India under the existing arrangements. Bangladesh, named as one of the two reserve teams alongside Oman, were subsequently invited to fill the vacant slot and accepted the offer. The revised six-team line-up comprises India, Japan, China, Malaysia, South Korea and Bangladesh. All league-stage matches will be played at the Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium in Jalandhar from October 27 to November 2, with the opening ceremony also scheduled at the venue. The semi-finals will be held in Mohali on November 4, while the final is scheduled for November 5 at the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium. Defending champions India, who won the title in Chennai in 2023 and Hulunbuir, China, in 2024, will open their campaign against Bangladesh on October 27. The scheduled India-Pakistan encounter on November 1 in Jalandhar has been scrapped following Pakistan’s withdrawal. First held in 2011, the Asian Champions Trophy has regularly featured the traditional rivalry between India and Pakistan. The two sides last met in the semi-finals of the 2026 Asian Games in Japan, where India secured a 4-3 victory before retaining the gold medal. Pakistan had also withdrawn from the Junior World Cup held in India last year, citing similar concerns. Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann had earlier indicated that Pakistan was expected to participate, referring to India’s policy of allowing neighbouring countries to compete in multi-nation sporting events. Despite Pakistan’s withdrawal and Bangladesh’s inclusion, the organisers have confirmed that the tournament will proceed as planned. The event will mark the return of a major international hockey tournament to Punjab after nearly two decades. The latest development highlights the continuing impact of political tensions on sporting ties between Pakistan and India, despite their longstanding association with hockey and efforts to promote the sport at the continental level.

𝐍𝐍𝐏𝐂 r𝐞𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐥 d𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 n𝐨𝐭 s𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐲 – Oyedele
items.description: …Says no 𝐏𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐜 𝐌𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐲 𝐈𝐧𝐯𝐨𝐥𝐯𝐞𝐝 Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, has said that the retail discount sale of fuel by the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) is not a subsidy. He provided the clarification in a statement in Abuja, today. According to him, “𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘥𝘪𝘴𝘤𝘰𝘶𝘯𝘵 𝘭𝘰𝘸𝘦𝘳𝘴 𝘱𝘳𝘪𝘤𝘦𝘴 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘴𝘶𝘮𝘦𝘳𝘴 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘤𝘢𝘯 𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘦𝘯𝘨𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘯 𝘕𝘕𝘗𝘊 𝘙𝘦𝘵𝘢𝘪𝘭’𝘴 𝘣𝘶𝘴𝘪𝘯𝘦𝘴𝘴 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘱𝘳𝘰𝘧𝘪𝘵𝘴 𝘢𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘢𝘮𝘦 𝘵𝘪𝘮𝘦. “Since 1 October 2026, motorists have been paying less for petrol at NNPC Retail Limited stations, following a discount on the company’s retail margin. We welcome the relief this brings to households, commuters and transporters. “Some commentators have described the discount as a return of fuel subsidy. That is not correct. Here, plainly, is what the discount is and what it is not.” 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧 d𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐚 s𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐲 a𝐫𝐞 n𝐨𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 s𝐚𝐦𝐞 “Every marketer adds a margin to the price it pays for the fuel it sells. A margin discount means the retailer chooses to take a smaller margin, or no margin at all for a period, and passes the saving to the customer. The cost of the discount is borne by the retailer alone. “A subsidy is different. It is when government pays part of the price the consumer would otherwise pay. That money comes from public revenue — funds that would otherwise go to salaries, schools, hospitals and infrastructure. That is the regime this administration ended in 2023, and it is not coming back. 𝐍𝐨 p𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐜 m𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐲 p𝐚𝐲𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐞 d𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 “The discount is not funded by the federal budget or the Federation Account. NNPC Retail buys petrol from the Dangote Refinery and other suppliers at market prices, on commercial terms, then adds its retail margin to set the pump price. The discount comes out of that margin alone, so the discounted pump price remains market-reflective. “This is quite different from crude oil owned by the Federation. Selling the nation’s crude below market price would amount to a subsidy, because the shortfall would be borne by public revenue.” 𝐃𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 n𝐨𝐭 e𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 r𝐞𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐞 𝐅𝐞𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐃𝐢𝐯𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐬 The Minister added that the NNPCL discount would nor affect Federation dividends the company would not lose any revenue. Mr. Oyedele said further, “Some have asked whether a lower margin means lower profits for NNPCL, and so lower dividends to the Federation. It need not. A smaller margin or temporary zero margin on each litre can be more than offset by selling more litres over time. “And a discount builds customer loyalty that lasts well beyond the discount period itself. Together, these can raise NNPC Retail’s profits, and the dividends paid to the Federation: a win-win for consumers and for government. Margin discounts are a routine commercial strategy, used by retailers the world over. 𝐃𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 won’𝐭 d𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐭 m𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐞𝐭 𝐨𝐫 e𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞 s𝐦𝐮𝐠𝐠𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠 “The retail margin on petrol is less than 5 percent of the pump price. A discount within that margin cannot meaningfully widen the gap between prices in Nigeria and in neighbouring countries, where petrol already costs 20 to 40 percent more. It therefore creates no new incentive for smuggling, and no distortion of the kind that subsidy regimes produced in the past.” The bottom line, according to the minister is that, “ 𝑨 𝒔𝒖𝒃𝒔𝒊𝒅𝒚 𝒔𝒑𝒆𝒏𝒅𝒔 𝒑𝒖𝒃𝒍𝒊𝒄 𝒎𝒐𝒏𝒆𝒚 𝒕𝒐 𝒍𝒐𝒘𝒆𝒓 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒑𝒓𝒊𝒄𝒆 𝒐𝒇 𝒇𝒖𝒆𝒍. 𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝑵𝑵𝑷𝑪 𝑹𝒆𝒕𝒂𝒊𝒍 𝒅𝒊𝒔𝒄𝒐𝒖𝒏𝒕 𝒍𝒐𝒘𝒆𝒓𝒔 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒑𝒓𝒊𝒄𝒆 𝒘𝒊𝒕𝒉𝒐𝒖𝒕 𝒔𝒑𝒆𝒏𝒅𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒂𝒏𝒚 𝒑𝒖𝒃𝒍𝒊𝒄 𝒎𝒐𝒏𝒆𝒚, 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒊𝒕 𝒄𝒂𝒏 𝒔𝒕𝒓𝒆𝒏𝒈𝒕𝒉𝒆𝒏 𝑵𝑵𝑷𝑪 𝑹𝒆𝒕𝒂𝒊𝒍’𝒔 𝒃𝒖𝒔𝒊𝒏𝒆𝒔𝒔 𝒂𝒕 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒔𝒂𝒎𝒆 𝒕𝒊𝒎𝒆. “ The post 𝐍𝐍𝐏𝐂 r𝐞𝐭𝐚𝐢𝐥 d𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 n𝐨𝐭 s𝐮𝐛𝐬𝐢𝐝𝐲 – Oyedele appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Former JoyNews journalist Ayisha Ibrahim called to the Bar
items.description: Former JoyNews journalist Ayisha Ibrahim has been called to the Ghana Bar, marking a significant milestone in her career in journalism and her pursuit of academic excellence. Ibrahim, who holds two master’s degrees, has added the title of Barrister and Solicitor of the Superior Court of Judicature of Ghana to her professional accomplishments after completing her legal training. She holds a Master of Laws (LL.M.) from the University of Ghana, where she deepened her knowledge of legal theory and jurisprudence, and a Master of Public Administration (MPA) from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). Her academic journey reflects an interest in law, governance, public administration and the workings of public institutions. The latest achievement follows years of balancing the demands of a journalism career with the rigorous academic requirements of legal education at the Ghana School of Law. The process required her to manage her professional responsibilities alongside the demands of legal studies, including extensive reading, case analysis and preparation for examinations. Describing the journey as difficult but rewarding, Ayisha’s achievement represents the culmination of years of academic commitment and professional development. Her call to the Bar marks a new chapter in her career, bringing together her experience in journalism and her training in law and public administration. Ibrahim’s journey also highlights the possibility of pursuing further education while maintaining a demanding professional career, offering encouragement to young people seeking to advance their education and careers. Her achievement has been celebrated as a testament to perseverance, discipline and a commitment to continuous learning. “Your dreams are valid, no matter how long the road,” she told Myjoyonline.com.
