items.title: NAF still searching for black boxes of crashed aircraft
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has commenced efforts to recover the flight data recorder and cockpit voice recorder of its ATR-42 aircraft that crashed in Igbokoda, Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, on Monday. The aircraft, with tail number NGR 931, was on a routine flight from Benin to Lagos when it crashed into a swamp opposite the Naval Forward Operating Base (FOB) in Igbokoda. All 25 personnel aboard the aircraft, including crew members, died in the crash. Five days after the accident, the main wreckage was yet to be excavated, while the remains of the victims were yet to be fully recovered. This is despite the deployment of heavy-duty amphibious excavators, known as swamp buggies, to the crash site. Only fragments of the aircraft had been recovered as of Saturday. The heavy equipment, deployed by the Ondo State Government, arrived alongside technical personnel armed with specialised detection equipment to pinpoint the location of the submerged wreckage. The swampy terrain, located about 500 metres east of the naval base, has made access and recovery particularly challenging, with initial attempts using small boats and canoes proving inadequate. Speaking at the crash site on Saturday, the NAF Superintendent of Standards and Evaluation, Air Vice Marshal Ebimobo Ebiowe, said investigators were searching for critical components of the wreckage that could help establish the circumstances surrounding the tragedy. Ebiowe identified the flight data recorder (FDR), commonly known as the black box, and the cockpit voice recorder (CVR) as key components investigators hoped to recover. He said, “We hope to be able to find critical components of the aircraft that will speak to the investigators because the aircraft wreckage actually speaks to the investigators. “One of them is what the ordinary man (civilian) calls the black box. We call it the flight data recorder (FDR), and another component close to it, the cockpit voice recorder (CVR).” The recorders are expected to provide crucial evidence to help investigators reconstruct the aircraft’s final moments and determine the factors that led to the crash. Aviation experts also said recovering and analysing the devices could provide important clues to the cause of the accident, although their findings would need to be assessed alongside other evidence from the wreckage and crash site. One of the experts, Mr Olugbenga Afolabi, said the recorders were among the critical components investigators would be looking for. He said the flight data recorder captured information about an aircraft’s performance and flight parameters, while the cockpit voice recorder preserved cockpit conversations, alarms and other sounds that could help investigators understand the crew’s actions before the crash. Meanwhile, the Nigerian Navy has deployed specialised sonar equipment to locate the submerged aircraft as recovery operations continue. The Chief of the Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Idi Abbas, directed the Nigerian Navy Hydrographic Department to deploy personnel and advanced sonar-scanning equipment to obtain an underwater picture of the crash site. Abbas said the deployment became necessary because of the swamp’s high turbidity, which had made underwater visibility extremely difficult. The Commanding Officer of the Officers’ Mess at the Forward Operating Base, Igbokoda, Navy Captain Andy Alemongwa, who received the personnel, said the sonar survey would help map the crash site and establish the precise location of the submerged aircraft. Alemongwa explained that the information would guide divers and other technical personnel involved in the recovery operation. The operation is also being supported by Nigerian Navy divers and NAF drone pilots conducting searches across the surrounding mangrove and forested areas, he said. The Flag Officer Commanding, Western Naval Command, Rear Admiral Abubakar Abdullahi Mustapha, and the Air Officer Commanding, Logistics Command, NAF, Air Vice Marshal Abubakar Abdul Suleh, have also visited the crash site. Air Chief: We’ll get to bottom of crash Earlier, the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, assured Nigerians that the military would conduct a comprehensive investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the crash and prevent a recurrence. Aneke, who appealed to the public to avoid speculation, said a high-level team comprising military and civilian aviation safety experts had been constituted to investigate the incident. He said the team would include safety specialists, representatives of the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau, the Accident Investigation Bureau, emergency management agencies, retired senior military officers and experienced NAF personnel. According to him, the team would examine the circumstances of the crash and establish what went wrong. “I have inspected the crash site, and I want to use this opportunity to thank the good people of Ondo State and our governor. They have committed resources, time and energy,” Aneke said. “I had informed my Superintendent of Safety and Evaluation to come up with a high-level delegation comprising both military and civilian safety experts, the NTSB, Accident and Emergency Management Board, retired senior officers and experienced Air Force officers, to sit down and get to the bottom of what happened,” he added. Aneke urged Nigerians to allow specialists to complete their investigation, describing the deaths of the personnel as a tragedy for the armed forces and the country. “This is not the time to start speculating, and I plead with the general public. We’ve lost people who are fighting for the nation. The best we can do for them is to be a little bit patient and let those who are specialists get to the bottom of what has happened,” he said. The Air Chief added that the NAF remained committed to safety, noting that aviation operations required rigorous attention to potential risks. He also disclosed that he and members of his family had previously flown in the same aircraft, expressing grief over the deaths of the crew members, whom he described as highly trained and professional officers. “I basically knew everyone on that flight. I have flown on this aeroplane. My family has flown on this aeroplane. I know each of the crew personally. They are highly trained, professional and intelligent officers. “The best we can do is to honour the sacrifice they have made for those on board this aeroplane,” Aneke said. The post NAF still searching for black boxes of crashed aircraft appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: « Sahraouis pour la paix » brise le monopole du polisario à l'ONU
items.description: Pour la deuxième fois devant la Quatrième Commission de l'ONU, « Sahraouis pour la paix » réclame que la recherche d'une solution ne soit plus réduite au seul polisario, qui prétend représenter à lui seul les Sahraouis. À New York, deux discours se sont croisés cette semaine devant la Quatrième Commission de l'Assemblée générale. Mardi, le représentant du polisario a ressorti la rhétorique habituelle du front séparatiste : un « représentant légitime et unique » du peuple sahraoui, qui exige l'« autodétermination et l'indépendance ». Deux jours plus tard, une délégation du mouvement « Sahraouis pour la paix », venu pour la deuxième fois, s'y présente avec une tout autre exigence, celle d'ouvrir le dossier du Sahara marocain à toutes les voix sahraouies. Cette posture du polisario ne trouve aucun appui dans les textes. La Cour de justice de l'Union européenne a rappelé, dans son arrêt du 4 octobre 2024 sur l'accord agricole (affaires C-779/21 P et C-799/21 P), que le polisario n'a jamais été officiellement reconnu comme représentant exclusif du peuple du Sahara. Son paragraphe 89 ne lui accorde qu'une place d'interlocuteur dans le processus onusien chargé de statuer sur l'avenir du territoire. Les résolutions de l'Assemblée générale vont dans le même sens : la 34/37 du 21 novembre 1979 (paragraphe 7) et la 35/19 du 11 novembre 1980 (paragraphe 10) le citent comme représentant du peuple du Sahara et lui ouvrent la voie de la négociation avec le Maroc, mais ne lui attribuent nulle part un monopole, que le front séparatiste et l'Algérie, qui reprend ses thèses, continuent pourtant de brandir. La légitimité que le polisario s'attribue est d'ailleurs contestée par plusieurs rapports internationaux, qui soulignent qu'aucune élection identifiable n'est à l'origine de sa direction. Ils pointent aussi le manque de transparence et de démocratie dans ses décisions sur le sort des Sahraouis, en particulier de ceux retenus à Tindouf. En face, « Sahraouis pour la paix » a vu le jour en 2020 autour d'anciens membres du polisario. Il a déjà fait savoir qu'il accepte l'initiative d'autonomie proposée par le Maroc comme socle d'un règlement négocié. Le mouvement plaide pour le pluralisme politique et pour le droit des Sahraouis à s'organiser dans des cadres alternatifs, sans se poser en porte-parole de tous, à la différence du polisario. Selon un communiqué du mouvement, sa délégation prend la parole jeudi et vendredi pour défendre l'option pacifique et politique qu'il porte depuis sa création. Il estime que l'évolution récente de l'approche internationale du dossier du Sahara rapproche les solutions envisagées de son propre modèle, fondé sur le dialogue, la négociation et la participation de toutes les voix sahraouies à un règlement réaliste et durable. Il demandera donc que cette dynamique serve à relancer le processus onusien, et que la séance du Conseil de sécurité attendue fin octobre élargisse les consultations politiques aux Sahraouis favorables à une solution négociée. Le mouvement affirme avoir gagné l'oreille de plusieurs acteurs internationaux, au premier rang desquels les États-Unis, dont des responsables ont reçu ses représentants pour entendre son projet. Il se présente comme une force sahraouie qui défend une solution tenant compte des intérêts de la population et ouvrant à tous la possibilité de participer à l'élaboration du règlement. Cette seconde participation à la Quatrième Commission, l'instance qui transmet ses recommandations à l'Assemblée générale, s'inscrit, dit-il, dans un effort continu pour s'imposer dans les enceintes internationales et faire entrer son approche dans les débats onusiens sur l'avenir du Sahara. Pour rappel, le représentant permanent des États-Unis auprès de l'ONU a reçu, le 30 juin dernier, une délégation de la direction du mouvement, composée du premier secrétaire, de deux membres du comité politique permanent et du responsable des relations extérieures. Les émissaires ont exposé leur vision du règlement de la question du Sahara, un conflit qu'ils décrivent comme un héritage de la guerre froide, et salué l'intérêt de Washington pour une issue pacifique. Ils ont aussi remis à l'ambassadeur et à ses collaborateurs un mémorandum retraçant l'évolution du dossier depuis ses origines, en lien avec leur position sur la vision américaine d'un règlement final. Le diplomate a ensuite écrit sur X avoir rencontré des voix sahraouies attachées à la paix, au compromis et à une solution durable, estimant que le monde devrait les écouter. The post « Sahraouis pour la paix » brise le monopole du polisario à l'ONU appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Counting performances of the Black Stars – at the doom stage?
items.description: Before the Black Stars went to the 2026 World Cup, news that circulated in the media was that the team needed a coach who commands respect in the dressing room and could give the team shape and a playing identity. It was on this basis that Coach Carlos Queiroz was appointed, and indeed we saw a little bit of his style against Wales in the 2026 pre-World Cup warm-up game. Ghanaians were hopeful after the Wales game and remained confident that Carlos Queiroz could orchestrate something against Panama- Blacks Stars’ first opponent in their 2026 World Cup group. Ghanaians were given anxious moments until that swift counter-attacking goal engineered by Caleb Yirenkyi and Antoine Semenyo to find Brandon Thomas Asante, who centered for the overlapping Yirenkyi at the near post to beat Panama 1-0 late in their first 2026 World Cup group game. The Black Stars demonstrated masterclass defending to hold England to a 0-0 stalemate in their second 2026 World Cup group game before succumbing 2-1 to Croatia in a technically flawed game, many assumed, in their third and final game of the group. The round of thirty-two (1/32) game the Stars lost to Colombia could have given game experts a clue about what this Black Stars team was lacking. The Ghanaian team demonstrated identical flaws in their 0-2 loss to Ivory Coast in an AFCON 2027 qualifier, an indication that, over a two-month break after the 2026 World Cup, the side had not provided any lessons to the side nor added anything at all. The brilliant defensive shape against England at the 2026 World Cup was entirely gone, and the solitary goal ammunition delivered against Panama couldn’t be replicated against the Ivorians in Bouake. Sincere Ghanaian football fans should have been sincere with themselves after the Ivory Coast game that this Black Stars team may have nothing to offer against Gambia. Yet false hopes and overwhelming confidence in the Black Stars in the past were hoped against hope before the Gambian game in Accra. The disappointing loss to Ivory Coast in the AFCON 2027 qualifier may have made an urgent call to defeat the Scorpions from Gambia. After taking a welcome 2-0 lead, the Black Stars slacked to two quick goals from the Gambians before conceding a third and eventually a fourth to fall comprehensively to a very determined Gambian side. The nation was shocked at the defeat. What does this explain about the current coach and the Black Stars team we have? The two goals against Gambia that mainly came through set pieces suggested that the present Black Stars team have still not grown in understanding of themselves on the pitch, which has a tendency to generate multiple scoring chances and goals to win games convincingly. The other option was to have carved into that stalwart defensive shape they exhibited against England at the 2026 World Cup at least, to concretely preserve the two-goal lead which could have been enough for any tactically good side to survive the ninety minutes without struggle. There was no identity after scoring the two goals as the Black Stars allowed the Gambians space to win more possession and cancelled the two-goal lead. Even at two-all (2-2), a technically effective coach could have decided to end the game in a draw at worst with a solid game approach that can prevent the Gambians from getting a third. If anyone should get a third goal, it should have been the Black Stars, whose followers were desperate for a win after the Ivory Coast loss. Passion to win for the nation was the only thing that could have saved a victory for Ghana, yet the country was represented by a batch of players that lacked drive and the personal will to save the day for Ghana. Personnel with the skill to transform games were entirely missing on the pitch of play, as observed by media personnel in an analysis after the game. Where does the Black Stars go from here? Until something is radically done, it will be very difficult for an average Ghanaian to express confidence in the Black Stars before they play Somalia. What can they offer? This sort of performance can continue if the entire team is not replaced with players who can ‘die’ on the pitch. Any top coach across the globe can have nothing to do about this team if they cannot inspire themselves on the pitch, even if he possesses the best strategies to win games. Yes, Carlos Queiroz may be partly to blame because he was the coach, but national team players who know their duty on the pitch could have definitely offered something better. A whole national orientation is needed for the present Black Stars team. Our recruitment strategy across the administration and the playing body and how we choose our coaches is reserved for another day.

items.title: Razaullah, Imran Randhawa handed debuts as Sri Lanka win toss, bat first against Pakistan in first T20
items.description: Pakistan handed Twenty20 International caps to all-rounders Razaullah and Imran Randhawa as Sri Lanka won the toss and elected to bat first in the opening fixture of the three-match series at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Friday. Both Razaullah and Imran made their Test debuts in the third and final Test against England last month. It was the former, however, who made it a memorable outing for himself, scoring a quickfire 81 in Pakistan’s second innings after having taken four wickets in the first. Imran, a domestic cricket veteran, on the other hand, took two wickets in that match, but comes into the Pakistan T20 side with the experience of 70 domestic games in the format. The right-handed batter and right-arm medium pacer put on show some crucial performances for Multan Sultans in this year’s Pakistan Super League season. The Sri Lanka series marks Sahibzada Farhan’s first assignment as Pakistan’s full-time T20 captain after leading the national side at the recent Asian Games, where Pakistan won a silver medal after losing to India in the final. The 30-year-old opener, who has played 48 T20Is, said on Thursday that he was excited about leading Pakistan on home soil and confident that the new combination could produce results. “This is the first time I am representing my country as a captain. It is a great honour for me,” Farhan told reporters at a pre-series press conference. “There is pressure, but it is not that we will let that pressure sit on our heads.” He said his experience of leading domestic sides and the Asian Games team had prepared him to handle the demands of captaincy. Farhan’s elevation is the most visible sign of a wider change in Pakistan’s T20 setup. Established names Babar Azam, Mohammad Rizwan and Shaheen Shah Afridi are absent, while Salman Ali Agha has also been removed from the T20 leadership group. Farhan, however, said the doors remained open for senior players. “Babar and Rizwan are experienced players and have remained among the world’s best. They can return to the national side anytime,” he said. “This is the Pakistan team; it doesn’t belong to anyone. Doors are open for everyone.” Pakistan are expected to adopt a more aggressive approach, with Farhan indicating that the likes of Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub, Hasan Nawaz and Maaz Sadaqat would be enc­o­uraged to play an attacking brand of cricket. The squad contains a blend of youth and experience. Fakhar and Shadab Khan provide seniority, so does Naseem Shah, who is also returns to T20I cricket after his last appearance against Sri Lanka during the T20 World Cup in February. Teams: Sri Lanka: Kusal Mendis (captain/wicket-keeper), Lahiru Udara, Kamil Mishara, Kamindu Mendis, Sahan Arachchige, Dasun Shanaka, Dunith Wellalage, Maheesh Theekshana, Dushmantha Chameera, Eshan Malinga, Nuwan Thushara Pakistan: Sahibzada Farhan (captain), Saim Ayub, Maaz Sadaqat, Fakhar Zaman, Hasan Nawaz, 6 Khawaja Nafay (wicket-keeper), Shadab Khan, Imran Randhawa, Razaullah, Naseem Shah, Abrar Ahmed

items.title: El último director de la Guardia Civil con el PP defiende su orden de archivar el ‘caso Cuarteles’
items.description: El juicio que se sigue en la Audiencia Provincial de Madrid por el llamado caso Cuarteles , que destapó supuestas irregularidades en la adjudicación de obras de rehabilitación en instalaciones de la Guardia Civil, ha escalado este viernes al ámbito de la política. José Manuel Holgado, que fuera el último director general de la Guardia Civil de los Gobiernos de Mariano Rajoy, ha declarado como testigo en la vista para explicar por qué, en diciembre de 2017, dio la orden de archivar la investigación abierta y que no se diera traslado de ella a la Fiscalía pese a que al menos dos informes apuntaban a la existencia de las anomalías en la contratación que finalmente han llevado al banquillo de los acusados al teniente general Pedro Vázquez Jarava , antiguo responsable de gestionar los recursos financieros y patrimoniales de la institución, y el empresario Ángel Ramón Tejera de León, alias Mon . Holgado, magistrado y actual presidente de la Sección Tercera de la Audiencia Provincial de Sevilla, ha asegurado que tomó aquella decisión porque entonces no vio indicios de delito, solo una mala praxis administrativa, y que, además, lo hizo “con conocimiento” de sus subordinados, en un intento de descargar su responsabilidad. items.title: When The Gospel boarded a trotro
items.description: By Jimmy Aglah Once upon a time in the Republic of Uncommon Sense, a man boarded a trotro at Kejetia with a Bible, a powerful voice and an urgent assignment from Heaven. His mission was to save souls before the vehicle reached Ejisu. Unfortunately, the passengers had boarded with entirely different expectations. Some wanted to sleep, others wanted to make telephone calls, and one exhausted woman simply wanted to reach home without being reminded that the wages of sin are death. The preacher, however, was not interested in their travel arrangements. Having obtained the driver’s permission, he considered the entire vehicle spiritually available for immediate redemption. He rose from his seat, cleared his throat and announced that everybody should prepare to meet the Lord. A gentleman seated behind the driver politely explained that he was only preparing to meet his wife, who had been waiting for him since morning. That was when the trouble began. The preacher reminded him that Jesus commanded His followers to go into the world and preach the Gospel. The gentleman agreed but wondered whether the instruction included compelling thirty unwilling passengers to attend an unscheduled church service. After all, he had paid for transportation, not theological instruction. This imaginary encounter captures the controversy currently exercising the Republic. Under Ghana’s Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519), preaching and hawking in moving public or commercial vehicles are prohibited. Offenders risk fines ranging from GH¢120 to GH¢600, imprisonment for up to eight months, or both. Interestingly, the prohibition is not new. It existed under L.I. 2180 in 2012. For 14 years, the law appears to have been travelling quietly in the boot while preachers occupied the passenger compartment. Now that enforcement has attracted renewed attention, some people are behaving as though Parliament has just deleted the Great Commission from the Bible. Prophet Nigel Gaisie has entered the controversy with considerable enthusiasm. He has announced his intention to preach aboard buses and lorries, daring the authorities to arrest him. He wonders what injury anyone suffers when the Gospel is preached and argues that preachers ordinarily obtain permission from drivers. The prophet raises an interesting question, but his answer creates an even more interesting problem. Since when did the driver become the constitutional representative of everybody’s conscience? A driver’s permission may authorise someone to enter his vehicle, but does it automatically authorise that person to convert every passenger into a member of an involuntary congregation? If that principle were universally accepted, a traditional priest could obtain the driver’s permission to perform rituals throughout the journey. A Muslim cleric could lead prayers over the same captive audience. A political activist could deliver a two-hour lecture on why his party deserves another opportunity to govern. And everybody would be expected to listen because the driver said yes. The Constitution guarantees freedom of religion under Article 21. But Article 12 also requires respect for the rights of others and the public interest. Religious freedom is precious, yet its exercise cannot be considered in isolation from the freedoms of fellow citizens. Surely, the right to preach deserves protection. So does the right to decline an invitation to be preached to. Meanwhile, Reverend Kwadwo Boateng Bempah has also condemned the restriction, insisting that the Church must continue proclaiming its message wherever people gather. It is a position rooted in religious conviction. Yet even within Christianity, opinion is divided. Reverend Enoch Paul Hayes of the International Central Gospel Church has reportedly urged fellow pastors to respect the law and explore alternative platforms for evangelism. Which introduces another fascinating question: If the Gospel can reach millions through radio, television, social media and organised outdoor evangelism, must salvation necessarily travel in a moving trotro ? To be fair, not every bus preacher is a nuisance. Some deliver thoughtful messages, offer encouragement to distressed travellers and conclude their sermons respectfully. Others have apparently mastered the remarkable art of turning a twenty-minute journey into a three-hour crusade, complete with testimonies, altar calls and financial appeals. The passenger who boarded at Kejetia hoping to reach Ejisu may consequently arrive spiritually exhausted before becoming physically exhausted. Nevertheless, the punishment deserves serious examination. Eight months in prison is a substantial maximum sentence for preaching in a moving vehicle. Public order matters, but proportionality matters too. Is imprisonment of that duration an appropriate possible response to conduct that may range from persistent harassment to an otherwise peaceful sermon delivered in the wrong setting? Surely, a civilised society can debate reasonable restrictions without automatically treating every offending preacher as a dangerous criminal. Consistency also matters. If excessive noise and passenger discomfort are the concerns, authorities must address other disruptive activities fairly. A passenger subjected to deafening music deserves consideration just as much as one trapped inside an unsolicited sermon. The central issue is neither Christianity nor hostility towards religion. It is the delicate business of sharing public space in a society where everybody has rights, convictions and destinations. We must avoid creating a country where every regulation becomes religious persecution and every expression of faith becomes a public nuisance. Perhaps the solution is remarkably simple: preach with consideration, listen by choice, enforce the law reasonably and remember that even the most righteous journey requires respect for fellow travellers. After all, Jesus invited people to follow Him. He did not appoint the trotro driver to accept the invitation on their behalf. And if the Lord Himself stands at the door and knocks, surely His earthly messengers can learn the courtesy of waiting for someone to open it.

items.title: Gender Ministry, IOM build stakeholders’ capacity to combat human trafficking in tourism and sports
items.description: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection (MoGCSP), in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration (IOM), has brought together stakeholders from the tourism, travel and security sectors to strengthen efforts to identify, prevent and respond to human trafficking. According to a post shared on Facebook on Friday, October 9, the two-day Capacity Enhancement and Awareness Raising Session on Human Trafficking in, Around and Through Tourism and Sports, held from Wednesday, September 30 to Thursday, October 1 focused on vulnerabilities associated with travel, recruitment, tourism and sporting activities, as well as measures to prevent exploitation and improve victim protection. The programme, organised through the Ministry’s Human Trafficking Secretariat, highlighted the potential exploitation of legitimate travel and sporting activities by traffickers to facilitate the movement and abuse of vulnerable people. In a keynote statement delivered on her behalf by the Ministry’s Chief Director, Dr Marian W. A. Kpakpah, the Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, called for greater public awareness, ethical recruitment practices and effective referral mechanisms to identify people at risk and ensure they receive appropriate protection and support. Dr Lartey stressed that human trafficking was not merely a criminal justice issue but also an assault on human dignity, freedom and fundamental human rights, requiring coordinated action across sectors. She also emphasised the need for transparent and responsible recruitment for employment, travel and sporting opportunities, urging that individuals be given accurate information about opportunities, terms and conditions. Representatives from the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Ghana Tourism Authority, Ghana Tourism Federation, travel and tour agencies and other relevant institutions participated in the engagement. Discussions covered the links between human trafficking, migration, tourism and child exploitation, alongside victim identification and protection, the National Referral Mechanism, ethical recruitment, trafficking in sports, safeguarding and child protection. Participants also conducted sector-specific risk mapping exercises for tourism, sports, travel and recruitment, identifying vulnerabilities and examining their respective roles in strengthening prevention, protection, referrals and responses.

items.title: FG targets five million Nigerians for poverty exit
items.description: …trains 700 Oyo youths in AI, vocational skills By Adeola Badru The Federal Government has launched an expanded poverty reduction initiative targeting five million Nigerians over the next four years, with 700 youths trained in artificial intelligence (AI), graphics design and vocational skills in Oyo State. The intervention, implemented through the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Technical, Vocational and Entrepreneurship Education (OSSAP-TVEE), is designed to tackle unemployment, bridge the skills gap and equip beneficiaries with the tools to establish businesses and participate in the digital economy. The Oyo training programme, which ran from September 28 to October 9, 2026, ended on Friday with a graduation ceremony at the Kensington Adebutu Hall, University of Ibadan, where participants received equipment and digital devices to support their transition from training to income-generating activities. Speaking at the ceremony, the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Technical, Vocational and Entrepreneurship Education, Dr Abiola Arogundade, said the initiative reflected President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to tackling poverty by creating opportunities for economic independence rather than relying solely on direct assistance. “What we want to do, and what the President wants to do, is to move as many people out of poverty as possible. “Mr President believes that our young people do not simply need assistance. They need opportunity. They need skills. They need the tools to compete and build sustainable livelihoods. And that is what today represents,” Arogundade said. She said the programme was structured to provide young Nigerians with practical competencies and equipment to transform their knowledge into viable businesses, as the Federal Government pursues its target of lifting five million people out of poverty within four years. Under the Oyo phase, 30 participants received specialised training in AI and graphics design, while 85 were trained in make-up artistry and another 85 in fashion design. An additional 500 participants received digital devices to support their participation in the growing digital economy. The beneficiaries received laptops, make-up kits, sewing machines and digital tablets, depending on their areas of training and the support provided. Arogundade urged the graduates to use the skills and equipment to build sustainable livelihoods and extend the benefits of the intervention to their communities. “What you receive today is not the destination. It is the beginning. Take the skills you have learnt. Take the tools you have received, and build something with them. “Don’t use it as a one-man solution or one-man empowerment. There’s a multiplier effect. Train your neighbours, train your community people, and also continue to impact and learn more,” she said. The Federal Government’s strategy emphasises practical skills, entrepreneurship and digital capabilities, with the intervention aimed at preparing beneficiaries for employment and self-employment in sectors where technology and specialised vocational knowledge are increasingly important. According to OSSAP-TVEE, the nationwide rollout will extend the programme beyond Abuja, where the initial pilot was conducted, and Oyo State. Subsequent phases are expected to cover other geopolitical zones, with 1,200 participants targeted per phase and training tailored to the needs of different regions. The keynote speaker and Principal Consultant, Mrs Oluronke Shonubi, said training young Nigerians in AI was important as major economies continued to integrate the technology across different sectors. “Countries such as the United States and China are investing heavily in AI across sectors including manufacturing, agriculture, and the automobile industry,” Shonubi said. She commended the government’s decision to expose young people to the technology and its ethical application, saying the knowledge could broaden their career options and create opportunities for entrepreneurship. Similarly, the make-up artistry instructor, Rukayat Muhammad, said the skills acquired could provide beneficiaries with a pathway to financial independence if properly developed and marketed. “Make-up artistry remains a marketable vocation, and beneficiaries can build successful businesses if they develop their skills and effectively market themselves,” Muhammad said. She urged the trainees to regard the equipment provided as an investment in their economic future and use it to establish and grow their businesses. The APC governorship candidate in Oyo State, Senator Sharafadeen Alli, urged the beneficiaries to see the training as a foundation for economic independence and use their skills to create employment opportunities for themselves and others. He said initiatives that equipped young people with practical skills and tools for establishing businesses were important to tackling unemployment and reducing poverty. “I urge all the beneficiaries to make the best use of this opportunity. The training and equipment provided are not just gifts; they are tools to build sustainable businesses, achieve financial independence and create employment for others. “The real success of this programme will be measured by how many lives are positively impacted beyond today,” Alli said. One of the beneficiaries, Olaleye Idowu, a 400-level International Relations student at the Federal University Oye-Ekiti, said the AI and graphics design training had introduced him to the fundamentals of the technology and its potential applications. “The training introduced us to the fundamentals of AI, its applications, and its potential to make work more efficient,” Idowu said. He said he hoped to become a professional AI prompt engineer within five years and pledged to train and employ others as his career progressed. “In five years, I expect to become a professional AI prompt engineer, and I pledge to train and employ others as I develop my career,” he added. Before the graduation ceremony, Arogundade led a presidential delegation on a courtesy visit to the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, who described the programme as a positive intervention in efforts to reduce poverty and empower young people. The monarch said initiatives that equipped beneficiaries with practical skills and opportunities to earn a living could help address socio-economic challenges at the grassroots. “It’s a very good initiative, and we are very proud of Arogundade,” Ladoja said. “I would also like to encourage many people in her position to emulate her, because this will go a long way in empowering people and reducing poverty in our society.” The ceremony attracted political figures and other stakeholders, including Alli’s deputy, Hon Michael Adesoji Adedeji; the senator representing Oyo Central, Yunus Abiodun Akintunde; the Oyo State APC Women Leader and Tinubu Torch Bearers coordinator, Dr Adekemi Felicia Opatunde; and the Southwest Federal Constituency coordinator, Hon Folake Olunloyo-Oshinowo. The post FG targets five million Nigerians for poverty exit appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le prix Nobel de la paix 2026 attribué à la Sud-Africaine Navanethem «Navi» Pillay
items.description: Le prix Nobel de la paix 2026 a été attribué, ce vendredi 9 octobre 2026, à la Sud-Africaine, la juriste de 85 ans Navanethem «Navi» Pillay, selon le comité Nobel. Elle obtient ce prix «pour ses efforts pour promouvoir la paix et le droit international». La juriste sud-africaine Navanethem «Navi» Pillay qui a présidé la commission d'enquête indépendante de l'ONU qui a accusé Israël de commettre un génocide dans la bande de Gaza, a remporté, ce vendredi 9 octobre 2026, le prix Nobel de la paix 2026. «La lauréate de cette année a joué un rôle déterminant pour garantir que les crimes de guerre, les crimes contre l'humanité et le génocide fassent l'objet de poursuites», a dit le président du comité Nobel norvégien à Oslo, Jorgen Watne Frydnes. Le jury a salué le «courage» et l’«intégrité» de la lauréate, soulignant qu’ «à une époque marquée par des défis existentiels – notamment un nombre de guerres et de conflits que le monde n'avait pas connu depuis longtemps –, le droit international n'est plus seulement un complément à la paix et à la sécurité». Navanethem «Navi» Pillay née d’une famille d’origine indienne, est devenue après ses études, avocate et pionnière du droit. «Un fil conducteur relie son travail précoce de défense de Nelson Mandela et d’autres qui se sont dressés contre l’apartheid à son rôle de juge dans certaines des affaires clés des tribunaux internationaux de notre époque », indique un communiqué du comité Nobel. Elle fut la première femme de couleur à siéger à la Cour suprême en Afrique du Sud avant de rejoindre le Tribunal pénal international pour le Rwanda. Par la suite Pillay a été juge à la Cour pénale internationale (CPI) de 2003 à 2008 et haut-commissaire des Nations unies aux droits de l’homme (HCDH) de 2008 à 2014. Navanethem Pillay est actuellement juge à la Cour internationale de justice dans l'affaire où la Birmanie est accusée de génocide. D’autres Africains ont déjà obtenu cette distinction dans le passé. Il s’agit, entre autres, Albert Lutuli (1960), Desmond Tutu (1984), Nelson Mandela et Frederik de Klerk (1993), Wangari Muta Maathai (2004) et Leymah Gbowee et Ellen Johnson Sirleaf (2011). Par Wakat Séra L’article Le prix Nobel de la paix 2026 attribué à la Sud-Africaine Navanethem «Navi» Pillay est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Our Fathers’ Affairs
items.description: We met by accident . I mean that literally—a Yankee friend of mine blew a tire while driving south and swerved into oncoming traffic. He came out of it untouched, and wound up in Atlanta while his car was being serviced. I live in Atlanta, and he called to see if I wanted to go out to dinner with him and his Aunt Maura to celebrate his survival. Maura was around my age and fairly new to town. We talked for a few minutes before dinner and she asked what I’d been writing. I told her I’d just finished a book about my father , Lou Junod. “What’s so interesting about him?” she asked, and I gave what had become my standard answer: “He was a philanderer.” And then, because that word didn’t seem to do Big Lou justice, I added the usual modifiers: charismatic, reckless, ruthless, relentless, irresistible, unrepentant, prolific. Maura’s reply did not require as many words. Her father also happened to be a philanderer, she said. But he wasn’t like that —he didn’t play the field. He was, by all appearances, an upright man. He just had a woman across town, and with her he had a second family, who knew him better than Maura’s family ever did, because at least the children the world deemed illegitimate knew his secrets. “It haunts me,” she said. “It haunts me, and it haunts my choices.” And then she asked the question that changed how I think about my father and men like him, perhaps men in general: “How many of us do you think are out there?” It was the us that threw me. I’d known almost all my life that my father was different from other fathers, both the comical ones I met in my neighborhood and the wise ones I watched on TV. When I was 3 years old, he had an affair with the mother of my first friend. When I was 6 or 7, he asked—he made a big deal of asking—if I wanted to go out for a hot-fudge sundae, and then stopped at a woman’s house on the way to the ice-cream parlor and left me outside on the swings. When I was in college, he invited me to New York City for a night on the town, and introduced me to one of his girlfriends. I was close with my brother, my sister, and my mother, but I never told them what I knew. I never told anyone. I was ashamed, of course—ashamed of him, ashamed of myself. But I was also proud. I had to be, because that’s what he demanded, that was our margin of survival. He made my mother cry. He made me cry too. But that wasn’t his fault; it was ours. It was, especially, mine. He didn’t do what he did because he was broken or weak or simply bad; he did it because he was special, a traveling salesman who, by virtue of his looks, his tan, and his insistence on his own virility, became a kind of bedroom celebrity, even to actual celebrities like the Gabor sisters. He did what other men wanted to do, what all men would do, if only they could, if only they weren’t so … weak. Did I want to be weak? No, anything but that. And so I made a faith of his faithlessness, believing that it, like Lou Junod himself, was unique. [ From the April 2019 issue: Sarah Zhang on the fertility doctor’s secret ] I knew what he did when he went on business trips for five or six weeks at a time or stayed overnight in Manhattan. But it took me a long time to find a language for what and who he was. He kept Playboy magazines in the drawer of his nightstand. Is that what he was, a playboy? Well, maybe, except that playboys weren’t supposed to be married to my mother. Was he a swinger? Nah—because he wasn’t countercultural, and he was above growing out his sideburns and wearing Nehru jackets. How about the words I encountered when I went to college and read Dostoyevsky, words such as sensualist and libertine ? That was more like it, because at least those words were classy, unlike the more readily available, the more down-and-dirty adulterer and cheat . I forget when I first came across philanderer . I remember that it struck me right away as a euphemism, a kind of excuse. Though rooted in Greek, it seemed French in intent, a description of a man with a pastime instead of a problem. It is a victimless crime of a word. Like multitudes of men and women throughout history, Lou Junod was promiscuous, lavishly and energetically so. But as a philanderer in good standing with the Oxford English Dictionary , he acquires a certain distinction—a set of linguistic cuff links for his custom-made shirts—that sets him apart and gives him what he was so skilled at making: a pass. Society has adopted philanderer as its word of choice for men like my father. But I did not write about him as such; I was careful to write about him as Dad rather than as a type. I doubt he’d appreciate having his secrets remorselessly exposed by his son in the pages of a book, but I believe he would give me credit for abiding by the terms of the silent pact we made so long ago. He would never be anything less than one of a kind. He would never be less than Big Lou. And so I was shocked when I met my friend’s Aunt Maura and with one question she turned the whole proposition upside down. “How many of us …” And there it was, the most impossible word for the child of a philanderer, the us that tells you you’re not alone. Don’t get me wrong—I liked the idea of having something in common with other people. I even liked the idea of being, well, a people , something larger than myself or even my family, a betrayed class, an entire woeful demographic. The only difficulty was that in seeing myself as part of an us , I had to see my father as part of a them , and I had invested so much of myself and my writing in the premise of his singularity. He was grubby and unglamorous as part of a group. He was typical—oh, let’s just say it, he was a typical male. He was not just unfaithful, he was not just promiscuous, he was not just an adulterer, he was not just a cheater, he was not just a philanderer—or, rather, he was just those things, and nothing more. He was run-of-the-mill. [ From the December 2019 issue: Tom Junod on his friend Mister Rogers ] And yet the question that Maura asked was not an idle one, not just a thought exercise. It has an answer, and I’ve been reminded of it nearly every day since publishing my book. I see them at the end of the signing line in bookstores, waiting patiently not just for an inscribed copy, but for the chance to speak the words that for most of their lives have been stalled at the tip of their tongue. I hear from them by email or direct message, the high-school classmates who write that they never knew I was just like them; the children of my father’s friends who tell me that I’ve told their stories as well as my own. And I meet them at parties, the acquaintances who become friends when they tell me about the news they received when they took their Ancestry.com tests; when they heard from the siblings they’d never known; when they found out about their father’s second or third family, or when they discovered that they were members of the second or third family and not, as they’d thought all their lives, the first and the only. How many of us are out there? I can say with great confidence that the answer is a lot , because I’ve gone out at last to meet the us , and it’s been the great belated gift of my growing-up to be able to speak with them, to be able to speak for them, and to know that what they want to tell me is often exactly what I want to tell them: I loved him. We are a wised-up lot, you see. We spent our innocence trying to believe in men we knew were guilty, only to find ourselves sometimes being employed as accessories and even collaborators in their crimes. But we always had one thing we could count on because we didn’t find it in our fathers’ closets, drawers, coat pockets, briefcases, or post-office boxes but rather in ourselves: our helpless love for the men who couldn’t stop breaking our hearts. And so when I’m out among them, my people, I hear myself saying it, and they hear themselves saying it, and we know it’s only a matter of time before we move on to the question we can’t answer: Did he ... ? And there’s something I hear myself saying often in response to this, in addition to my hopeful Yes . He was a good father, I say. He tried hard. He spent time with me. He always showed me affection. He never stinted on telling me he loved me. He was dedicated, he was dogged, he was determined. And that’s when I see that I’m at last surrounded by people who are not so different from me, who are just the same, and who know that everything I’m saying about Lou Junod as a father, I could be saying about Big Lou the philanderer. *Image sources: CSA-Printstock / Getty; GraphicaArtis / Getty; LMPC / Getty; Found Image Holdings / Corbis Historical / Getty; Jack Mitchell / Getty. This article appears in the November 2026 print edition with the headline “Our Fathers’ Affairs.”

items.title: Health Ministry declares Yellow Fever outbreak in Upper West Region
items.description: The Ministry of Health, working through the Ghana Health Service and in partnership with the World Health Organisation, has declared a Yellow Fever outbreak in some affected districts in the Upper West Region following laboratory confirmation of three cases, all of which resulted in deaths. In a statement issued on October 9, the Ministry said the outbreak follows reports of suspected cases presenting with fever, jaundice, and bleeding in health facilities from September 9 in Sissala West and Wa West. Samples were initially tested in the country, and further testing at the WHO-accredited laboratory in Dakar, Senegal, confirmed three cases due to yellow fever. All three cases resulted in deaths despite aggressive management by health staff. In line with the International Health Regulations (2005) and the National Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851), the Minister for Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, has declared a Yellow Fever outbreak in the affected districts. The Ministry, through the Ghana Health Service, has activated the National and Regional Public Health Emergency Operations Centres and deployed Rapid Response Teams to affected communities for case finding, surveillance, and risk communication. It is also preparing for a targeted emergency vaccination campaign in affected and at-risk districts, including Wa West, Sissala West, and Sissala East, this month of October. Other measures include promoting the use of insecticide repellents and sleeping under insecticide-treated bed nets during the day, strengthening case management at designated health facilities, heightened surveillance across the region, and intensified risk communication and community engagement activities. The Ministry advised the public to report to the nearest health facility immediately if they experience sudden fever, headache, muscle pain, yellowing of the eyes or skin, or unusual bleeding. It also urged the public to eliminate stagnant water around homes, use insecticide-treated nets and mosquito repellents, avoid self-medication, and rely only on official communication from the Ministry of Health and the Ghana Health Service. The Ministry called on traditional and religious leaders, the media, civil society, and all citizens to support the national response, and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the health and well-being of every person in Ghana.

items.title: CRS, LDS hand over 6 renovated NAS facilities to strengthen emergency response
items.description: Catholic Relief Services (CRS), with funding from The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (LDS), has handed over six renovated and expanded National Ambulance Service (NAS) facilities across northern Ghana to strengthen emergency referral and transport services. The facilities are located in the Talensi and Nabdam Districts in the Upper East Region, Mamprugu Moagduri District in the North East Region, Yendi and Nanumba North Municipalities in the Northern Region, and Central Gonja District in the Savannah Region. The intervention forms part of the three-year Holistic Opportunities for Positive Engagement in Maternal and Child Health (HOPE-MCH) Project, which seeks to improve maternal, newborn and child health by strengthening support at the family, community, health facility and health system levels. Speaking on behalf of the CRS Country Representative at the Talensi district handover ceremony, Health Program Manager at CRS Ghana, Adam Haliq, said strengthening emergency response systems was critical to ensuring timely access to lifesaving care. “Every minute matters when a mother, newborn, or child needs urgent medical attention,” he said, adding that the project was strengthening systems that connect people to lifesaving care, particularly in communities where distance and difficult terrain could delay access to timely care. Talensi District Chief Executive, John Millim Naabwomya, described the renovation of the National Ambulance Service Office as more than a physical upgrade, stressing the importance of collaboration among institutions and development partners in achieving sustainable development. “Our district ambulance was out of service for a long time. Under my leadership, we were able to mobilise resources to purchase an engine and other essential parts to repair it and get it back on the road”, he said. “Sustainable development is achieved when institutions and partners work together around a common purpose”. The Member of Parliament for Talensi, Daniel Mahama Dung, said efforts to restore and improve ambulance services in the area dated back to 2024. He explained that following the renovation of the facility, he supported efforts to address some of its immediate needs, including the provision of water, which he said was made available within two or three weeks. The MP called for continued support for healthcare delivery in the constituency, stressing that stakeholders should look beyond the ambulance service and support the wider health needs of the community. Receiving the facilities on behalf of the National Ambulance Service, Deputy Director for Policy, Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation, Dr Simon Akayire Nyaaba, expressed appreciation to CRS and LDS for supporting the Service. He said the improved offices, together with emergency vehicles and dispatch systems provided under the project, would strengthen the operational foundation of the National Ambulance Service and enable personnel to coordinate more effectively and respond to communities when emergency care is needed. As part of the wider HOPE-MCH intervention, CRS has also provided the National Ambulance Service with 40 Modified Motor-Tricycle Ambulances and 10 motorcycles to improve emergency response in hard-to-reach communities. The six renovated facilities complement these investments and are expected to improve the capacity of the National Ambulance Service to provide timely emergency referral and transport services, particularly for women, newborns and children in underserved communities.

items.title: Gunmen kill security operative in Plateau
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa Gunmen have reportedly killed a security operative on his way to his duty post along the Kwi-Beco road in Plateau State. The incident, according to sources, occurred at about 7pm on Thursday around Kwi, between Riyom and Barkin Ladi local government areas of the state. The security operative was reportedly travelling on a motorcycle to his duty post in the Chit area of Heipang when he was attacked and killed. Sources said the assailants also made away with the motorcycle after the attack. The spokesman of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association (BYM), Rwang Tengwong, confirmed the incident and described it as disturbing. Tengwong lamented that the killing of a security operative raised serious concerns about the safety of civilians in the affected communities. He said it was particularly troubling that security personnel deployed to protect residents were themselves vulnerable to attacks. The BYM spokesman condemned the killing and called for urgent measures to address the security challenges confronting communities in the area. Efforts to reach security operatives for official confirmation of the incident were unsuccessful as of press time. items.title: Gunmen kidnap three CRIN workers in Oyo, demand N120m ransom
items.description: By Adeola Badru Gunmen have abducted three people, including two staff members of the Cocoa Research Institute of Nigeria (CRIN), Idi Ayunre, in the Oluyole Local Government Area of Oyo State, and demanded N120 million for their release. The victims were identified as Mrs Eunice Babalola, leader of CRIN’s Central Nursery; Mr Kehinde Gbalajobi, an agricultural superintendent; and another man who resides in the institute’s SS Quarters but is not a member of staff. The abduction occurred during working hours yesterday, according to the information gathered by our correspondent. A source familiar with the incident disclosed that Babalola and Gbalajobi were kidnapped while walking from the institute’s Central Nursery to the SS Quarters, where Babalola intended to collect some items from her residence. The source explained that their driver was expected to pick them up at the quarters while returning from the nursery to the institute’s main office with other nursery staff. The two workers, however, were intercepted by the gunmen before they could reach the quarters, while the third victim, a resident of the SS Quarters who is not employed by CRIN, was also abducted. The source said the gunmen subsequently attempted to abduct additional people at the Central Nursery but were prevented from doing so following a fierce exchange of gunfire with security personnel on guard. “The kidnappers went to the Central Nursery to pick more victims but were repelled after a fierce exchange of gunshots with the security men on guard at the time,” the source said. The source further disclosed that the kidnappers had established contact with the victims’ relatives and were demanding a total ransom of N120 million for the release of the three abductees. The incident has raised fresh concerns over the safety of workers and residents within the institute’s premises, particularly following the reported attempt by the gunmen to seize additional victims. Confirming the incident, the Police Public Relations Officer in Oyo State, DSP Ayanlade Olayinka, said the victims were abducted while inspecting crops on a farm within the institute’s premises. According to the police spokesman, security operatives have commenced efforts to track down the perpetrators and secure the victims’ release. “A manhunt has been launched, and operational efforts are ongoing to ensure the victims’ safe return and bring those responsible to justice,” Ayanlade said. He added that the command was deploying the necessary resources to address the situation and appealed to members of the public to provide useful information that could assist the ongoing operation. “The command reassured the public that every necessary effort is being made to resolve the situation and urges anyone with credible information that could assist the ongoing operation to promptly report to the nearest police station or contact the command through its established emergency channels,” he said. Ends The post Gunmen kidnap three CRIN workers in Oyo, demand N120m ransom appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NLC/NUT strike: Wike threatens no-work, no-pay
items.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, has declared the ongoing strike by the FCT Chapter of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT) as political and baseless. Wike, who stated this after meeting with chairmen of the six area councils in Abuja on Friday, directed the council chairmen to enforce a strict “no-work, no-pay” policy against participating workers. He added that he had directed the council leadership to clamp down on unapproved absence. “We have directed the chairmen of the area councils to call their teachers and state clearly: if anybody participates in this, we will implement no-work, no-pay. “Enough is enough; we cannot continue with this,” Wike warned. The minister rejected the rationale behind the industrial action, asserting that all legitimate demands raised by the teaching body, including promotions and operational matters, had been substantially resolved or were actively being implemented. “We want to state categorically and let it be known to the public: this so-called strike declaration is political, and we will not accept it. “There is no basis for anybody to call for a strike. We don’t have any issue with the Local Education Authorities or primary schools. Everything we have agreed on, we are implementing,” he said. Wike noted that secondary school teachers and other key union segments had distanced themselves from the strike action, recognising that the demands were already being met. Addressing the political underpinnings of the shutdown, the minister directly challenged the political neutrality of the local NLC leadership. He alleged that the union chairperson was a former candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in the last February FCT area council elections. “You can see his interest. He is trying to ensure the FCT is in crisis as a political tool, telling voters that pupils are at home. We will not accept that blackmail. “If you want to involve yourself in politics, you are free to do so, but excuse yourself from holding union leadership so you don’t politicise it,” he advised. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) recalls that the NLC had on Wednesday directed workers of the FCT Administration and those in the private sector to begin indefinite strike over unresolved issues between the FCTA and NUT. The issues relate to NUT’s demand on the FCTA to withdraw the redeployment of some directors in agencies under the FCT Education Secretariat, rescheduling of 2025 promotion examination and removal of vacancy precondition for promotion. items.title: Labour Minister banks on dialogue to end teachers’ strike, rules out alternative measures
items.description: Labour Minister Emmanuel Kwadwo Agyekum has expressed confidence that dialogue will resolve the ongoing strike by three teacher unions, insisting that the government will not need to resort to alternative measures to compel teachers to return to the classroom. The Minister’s optimism follows an emergency meeting with representatives of the three teacher unions, as the government intensifies efforts to resolve the dispute over salary arrears owed to promoted teachers, conditions of service and other outstanding employment concerns. The strike has disrupted teaching and learning in public pre-tertiary schools, putting pressure on the government to reach an agreement with the unions and restore normal academic activities. Speaking to the media after the meeting on October 9, Mr Agyekum described the discussions as positive and expressed confidence that the parties would make significant progress towards ending the industrial action by the close of the day. “We’ve just finished with the teacher unions. It’s been a very positive meeting, and I strongly believe that by the close of the day we should be able to have a solution to this industrial action,” he said. He added that the negotiations had covered three key areas: the collective agreement, issues relating to teachers’ promotions and the payment of deprived-area allowances. According to the Minister, the parties had engaged in extensive discussions on the outstanding issues, raising hopes that a mutually acceptable resolution could be reached. Mr Agyekum said the depth of the discussions had strengthened his belief that the impasse could be resolved without the government resorting to more forceful measures. Asked whether the government was considering alternative steps to compel the teachers to return to work should negotiations fail, the Minister dismissed the possibility, insisting that the progress made so far made such an eventuality unlikely. He reiterated his expectation that a positive outcome would be communicated before the end of the day. “Positively, we’ll hear something by the close of today,” he added. For now, Mr Agyekum remains hopeful that the deadlock can be broken through dialogue, with a positive announcement expected by the close of the day. The unions began the indefinite industrial action on Friday, September 25, after a September 24 deadline for the government to address their concerns passed without a resolution. Their grievances include unpaid promotion-related arrears, delays in negotiating a new Collective Agreement and the implementation of the Deprived Area Allowance.

items.title: Transport operators slam gov’t; vow to defy suspension of preaching and hawking restrictions
items.description: The Commercial Transport Operators of Ghana have vowed to resist the government’s decision to suspend the implementation of Regulation 141 of Legislative Instrument (L.I.) 2519, insisting that preaching and hawking will not be permitted in vehicles operated by their members. The regulation restricts preaching, hawking and other activities d eemed a nuisance in moving public transport vehicles. A high-ranking government source confirmed the suspension to Myjoyonline.com amid public debate over the restrictions and concerns raised by religious leaders and other stakeholders. Read Also: Gov’t suspends implementation of L.I. restricting preaching and hawking in moving vehicles In a statement issued on October 9, the operators expressed disappointment with the government’s decision, arguing that the regulation was necessary to protect passengers’ safety and comfort during journeys. “We are disappointed in the government’s decision to ban Regulation 141,” the statement said. The group warned that it would oppose any attempt to suspend the regulation, maintaining that the restrictions would remain in force in its members’ vehicles despite the government’s position. “We will resist any attempt to suspend it. No preaching or hawking will be allowed in our vehicles,” the statement added. The operators are calling for the immediate enforcement of Regulation 141, arguing that it would help create a safer and more comfortable environment for passengers using public transport. Their stance puts them at odds with the government’s decision to suspend the regulation’s implementation and raises questions about how the restrictions will be applied in practice. The group has nevertheless maintained that it will prohibit preaching and hawking in its members’ vehicles, regardless of the government’s decision. The law has been in existence since 2012 but was not enforced until the recent amendment in 2026 that increased the punishment for offenders with a pledge to enforce it.

items.title: Domestic abuse is about power and control, not ordinary relationship conflict – ARK Foundation
items.description: The Executive Director of the ARK Foundation, Dr Angela Dwamena-Aboagye, has called for a better understanding of domestic abuse, warning that treating it as an ordinary disagreement between couples can prevent victims from receiving the support and protection they need. She said abuse was fundamentally about one person using a pattern of controlling, coercive and harmful behaviour to gain and maintain power over another, rather than simply two people disagreeing. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show during a discussion on why people remain in abusive relationships, Dr Dwamena-Aboagye said a failure to understand the nature of abuse often led people to confuse it with common arguments in marriages and relationships. When asked about the causes of domestic abuse and how society could address the problem, she said the need for people to understand what abuse entails before attempting to offer solutions. “If we don’t understand the phenomenon itself, we conflate it with many other things,” she said. “You know, for example, that it’s like people fighting in a relationship. But there’s a big difference between common household arguments, conflicts within marriages or relationships and violence.” She urged the public to take advantage of available information to learn about abusive behaviour and how it differs from ordinary relationship disagreements. “Let’s get knowledge and understanding about the phenomenon of abuse within relationships, within our homes, within marriages or families,” she said. Dr Dwamena-Aboagye explained that domestic abuse involves a pattern of behaviour through which an individual seeks to control another person and maintain dominance in a relationship. Defining an abuser, she said: “An abuser is a person who uses a pattern of coercive, controlling and harmful behaviors to gain and maintain power over an intimate partner, a family member or a dependent.” She urged the public to pay particular attention to the words pattern, coercive and controlling, saying these were central to understanding how abuse operates. “The dynamics are simple. I want to exercise power and control over you because I believe that I have that power and I can control you,” she said. According to her, this sense of entitlement may come from an individual’s beliefs about themselves, the culture in which they live, or the attitudes they learnt while growing up. She said understanding these influences was important because cultural beliefs can shape how people view relationships, including whether they believe one partner has the right to dominate or control the other. Without this understanding, she warned, people risk offering advice that fails to address the real problem. Dr Dwamena-Aboagye acknowledged that advice encouraging submissiveness or urging men not to beat their wives could be well-intentioned. However, she said such advice could be inadequate if it failed to recognise the underlying pattern of control in an abusive relationship. She explained that abuse was not simply a case of one partner reacting badly to something the other had done. Instead, it involved one person assuming the authority to control or harm the other. That imbalance can also affect how people interpret a victim’s response to violence. “In a relationship where there’s abuse, you would see a pattern of dominance. One person arrogates to themselves the power to do certain things against the other person,” she said.

items.title: Le mois de septembre 2026, le plus chaud enregistré au Maroc depuis 1981
items.description: Le Maroc vient de traverser un mois de septembre d'une anomalie thermique inédite. Selon un communiqué rendu public ce vendredi par la Direction générale de la météorologie (DGM), septembre 2026 s'est imposé comme le mois de septembre le plus chaud dans le Royaume depuis 1981, enregistrant un écart de température moyen de +2,75 °C par rapport à la normale climatologique de référence établie sur la période 1991-2020. Cette hausse exceptionnelle dépasse largement les précédents pics historiques recensés en septembre 1987 (+1,99 °C) et en septembre 2020 (+1,78 °C), conférant à cette période un caractère inédit dans les annales météorologiques nationales. D'après les analyses de la DGM, cette surchauffe s'explique par la conjonction de plusieurs facteurs synoptiques majeurs, notamment la remontée continue de masses d'air chaud d'origine tropicale et l'activation répétée des vents du Chergui véhiculant l'air saharien torride et sec vers l'ouest et le centre du pays. La persistance d'un puissant dôme de chaleur lié à de hautes pressions en altitude a également bloqué la formation de nuages tout en provoquant la compression et le réchauffement de l'air en basse atmosphère, alimentant ainsi des vagues de chaleur intenses. Cette dynamique a entraîné la chute de plusieurs records historiques à travers le réseau national. Dès le 3 septembre, la ville de Sidi Slimane a atteint un sommet absolu de 47,1 °C, surpassant son précédent record de 1988, tandis que Kénitra et Salé enregistraient respectivement 45,1 °C et 44,3 °C. Dans les provinces du Sud, la ville de Laâyoune a également franchi un nouveau cap le 8 septembre avec un pic mesuré à 45,8 °C. La Direction générale de la météorologie souligne que ces manifestations extrêmes s'inscrivent directement dans la trajectoire du réchauffement climatique global, marqué par la fréquence et l'intensification accrues des anomalies thermiques. L'instance insiste sur l'importance d'un suivi scientifique continu afin de fournir les données stratégiques indispensables à l'élaboration des politiques d'adaptation du Royaume. The post Le mois de septembre 2026, le plus chaud enregistré au Maroc depuis 1981 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Motorists, commuters, others react to FG’s 30-day petrol discount
items.description: Many motorists, commuters, and stakeholders have expressed mixed reactions to the Federal Government’s announcement of a 30-day petrol discount at the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Ltd. (NNPCL) filling stations. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele on Thursday announced the discount on petrol prices and subsidy-related issues in Abuja. Oyedele said the arrangement would run for 30 days, with public transport operators receiving priority nationwide. Mr Shehu Mohammed, a motorist who resides at Dutse, told NAN that the measure would reduce transportation costs and ease the financial pressure on households. Shehu said it would also provide relief amid rising petrol prices. Mr Wale Oshobu, a motorist who resides at Bwari, said the gesture was commendable but Nigerians do not know the actual discount consumers would receive and how it would translate into lower transport fares. Mr Dotun Ogunsola, a consumer, said, “Nigerians need sustainable solutions to fuel price volatility rather than temporary relief measures. “The effectiveness of the discount will depend on its size from NNPCL stations,” he said. Mrs Uche Ogor, a consumer who resides at Wuse, urged relevant stakeholders to monitor the transparency of the initiative and the Federal Government’s plans for the period after the initial 30 days. Mr Wumi Iledare, a Professor Emeritus of Petroleum Economics, Louisiana State University (LSU) Energy Institute, said the initiative could be defensible if it remained a targeted, temporary welfare intervention rather than a return to universal fuel subsidy. Iledare said the purpose should not be to make petrol artificially cheap, but to ease transport costs, limit their spillover into logistics and consumer prices. He said the initiative should provide short-term relief to vulnerable households. “Prioritising public transporters may be justified only if the savings ultimately reach passengers. “The decisive question is simple: who pays for the discount? If NNPC Ltd sells below economic cost and government later reimburses it or an implicit public liability arises. The measure is subsidy-equivalent. “The economics are different only if NNPCL transparently funds the discount from a commercial margin for a strictly limited period without creating a fiscal obligation. “Government should therefore disclose the discount per litre, eligible volumes, financing source, maximum fiscal exposure, mechanism for passing savings to passengers, and the final financial impact on NNPCL. “These are not merely accounting details; they determine whether the policy is genuine welfare support or subsidy through another channel,” he said. Mr Auwal Rafsanjani, the Executive Director of Civil Society Legislative Advocacy Centre (CISLAC), said the intervention risked becoming another temporary announcement that failed to address the suffering of citizens. Rafsanjani said Nigerians deserved accountability, not economic promises without measurable results. He called for transparency regarding the proposed N1,350 petrol price and the 30-day NNPCL discount. “What will Nigerians actually pay for the pump price of petrol? Who is financing the discount, how much will it cost, and what happens after 30 days? “ More importantly, how will this intervention reduce transportation fares, food prices and the cost of essential commodities across the country? “Government must explain where the savings from petrol subsidy removal have gone, how much was realised, and what measurable improvements will reach the ordinary Nigerians,” he said He called on the Federal Government to confront the real drivers of economic hardship, excessive governance costs, and policies that undermined businesses and livelihoods. According to him, government must demonstrate the same financial discipline and sacrifice it demands from citizens by cutting unnecessary expenditure, expanding affordable transportation and protecting vulnerable households. (NAN) The post Motorists, commuters, others react to FG’s 30-day petrol discount appeared first on Vanguard News .
