Keep your windows open or risk lung cancer – GAEC warns over deadly radon gas
items.description: The Ghana Atomic Energy Commission (GAEC) has warned Ghanaians about the risk of lung cancer from exposure to radon gas, urging households to improve ventilation by keeping windows open to prevent the radioactive gas from accumulating indoors. Radon is a naturally occurring radioactive gas produced by the decay of uranium in soil and rocks. It can seep into buildings from the ground and accumulate in poorly ventilated spaces, exposing occupants to potentially harmful levels of radiation. The Director of Radiation Protection at GAEC, Dr Eric Tetteh Glover, says radon is the second leading cause of lung cancer after smoking, particularly among non-smokers. Speaking during a visit by Environment Minister Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings to the Commission at Atomic in Accra, Dr Glover said GAEC is working with the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Ghana Standards Authority to introduce measures that will require radon assessments before buildings are constructed. He explained that the proposed measures would help identify areas with high radon concentrations and ensure buildings are designed to reduce exposure to the gas. Dr Glover said the Commission also intends to establish guidelines for construction in areas where radon levels are high, including requirements for adequate ventilation. Explaining the health risks, Dr Glover said radon becomes dangerous when inhaled, as its radioactive properties can damage lung tissue and increase the risk of cancer. “The effect of radon is lung cancer. The WHO says it is the second leading cause of lung cancer, especially in non-smoking people,” he said. He explained that once inhaled, radon and its radioactive decay products can expose the lungs to radiation, potentially contributing to the development of cancer. Dr Glover noted that radon testing is already part of building safety practices in some developed countries, where assessments are conducted before construction begins. “Radon testing should be conducted before construction begins. Unfortunately, Ghana does not yet have the necessary facilities for such testing,” he said. He said GAEC is working to establish the necessary capacity to support radon testing in Ghana and strengthen preventive measures against exposure. Dr Glover also raised concerns about miners who work underground for extended periods, saying the Commission is collaborating with the Minerals Commission and the Chamber of Mines to improve ventilation in mining environments. He explained that miners may spend about eight hours underground, making adequate ventilation important in reducing their radon exposure. The Commission’s warning highlights the need for greater public awareness of radon exposure and for building standards that help protect people in homes, workplaces and other enclosed spaces.

items.title: Binti Invest: Dominique Delafosse nommé vice-president Worldwide
items.description: La nomination de Dominique Delafosse comme vice-président Worldwide de la banque d’affaire Binti Invest, accompagne les ambitions internationales d’un groupe positionné sur l’ingénierie financière, le conseil stratégique et l’investissement, à la croisée des infrastructures, de l’énergie et des nouvelles technologies. Dominique Delafosse est nommé vice-président Worldwide de Binti Invest. Cette nomination intervient, opportunément, dans un groupe qui entend relier les capitaux internationaux aux projets de développement, avec un positionnement tourné notamment vers l’Afrique, le Moyen-Orient et l’Asie, et des implantations européennes destinées à soutenir ses activités transfrontalières. Ce titre de vice-président à l’échelle mondiale donne une dimension internationale aux nouvelles fonctions de Dominique Delafosse qui jouit, dans le monde des affaires, d’une réputation de «grand bosseur». Le périmètre précis de ses responsabilités, les modalités de sa prise de fonction et ses premières priorités devront toutefois être précisés dans la communication officielle accompagnant la nomination. Un groupe à la convergence du financement et des projets Binti Invest se présente comme un groupe international d’ingénierie financière, de conseil stratégique et d’investissement, dont le siège est situé à Mascate, au Sultanat d’Oman. Son ambition affichée est d’accompagner les gouvernements et les entreprises dans la définition, la structuration et la réalisation de leurs objectifs stratégiques. Son positionnement repose sur une approche intégrée: associer la recherche de financements, la structuration du capital, le conseil et les compétences nécessaires au développement des projets. Le groupe décrit ainsi une chaîne de valeur allant de l’idée initiale jusqu’à l’actif en exploitation, en passant par la levée de fonds, la conception et la construction. Binti Invest présente sept secteurs d’intervention: l’architecture, l’immobilier, l’intelligence artificielle et la technologie, la finance et les investissements, l’énergie, la défense et la sécurité, ainsi que le pétrole et le gaz. Cette diversité constitue le socle de son ambition, celle de faire travailler ensemble des expertises financières, techniques et stratégiques autour de projets de long terme. Un potentiel fondé sur la complémentarité des métiers Le potentiel de Binti Invest tient d’abord à cette capacité recherchée de rapprocher les besoins des porteurs de projets et les exigences des investisseurs. Dans son modèle affiché, le financement n’est pas dissocié de la conception technique, de la coordination opérationnelle ou de la stratégie de développement. Cette articulation peut constituer un atout pour accompagner des opérations complexes, notamment dans les infrastructures, l’immobilier et l’énergie. Le groupe présente plusieurs structures aux fonctions complémentaires. Binti-A, implantée à Paris et à Abu Dhabi, est décrite comme une plateforme de conseil et de coordination des mandats, intervenant notamment dans la structuration et les marchés de capitaux. Binti Invest Oil & Gas, établie à Mascate, se consacre au négoce d’hydrocarbures, à la structuration des cargaisons, à la logistique et à la gestion du risque. En France, Binti Triptyque est dédiée au développement et à la réalisation immobilière en Europe. Cette organisation dessine une proposition de valeur: combiner l’accès aux capitaux, la connaissance des marchés et l’exécution des projets. Elle décrit toutefois un potentiel et un positionnement stratégique, plutôt qu’une mesure de performance: les pages consultées ne fournissent pas de données permettant de quantifier les actifs gérés, les financements mobilisés ou le volume de projets effectivement livrés. Une équipe pluridisciplinaire à vocation internationale Pour porter cette ambition, Binti Invest met en avant une équipe réunissant des compétences en finance, ingénierie, technologie et affaires publiques sur plusieurs continents. Sa page officielle présente notamment I. Ahamed comme fondateur, M. Mockel comme directeur général, Y. Guillot comme vice-président Europe et D. Pingisi comme directeur international. Le dispositif comprend également des fonctions spécialisées: P. Sartorius est présenté comme conseiller stratégique en finance, D. Le Baut comme conseiller stratégique, J. Enseñat comme directeur des opérations pétrole et gaz, et S. Perez comme CEO de Binti Invest Oil & Gas. G. Bonneveau apparaît pour sa part comme associé et CEO de Binti Triptyque. Cette répartition illustre la volonté du groupe de réunir des profils de direction, de conseil et d’exécution sectorielle. L’ancrage international documenté relie notamment l’Europe, le Moyen-Orient et l’Afrique, tandis que l’Asie figure également parmi les zones prioritaires annoncées. Le groupe revendique une présence active sur quatre continents, sans que les éléments consultés permettent d’identifier précisément un réseau d’experts établi en Amérique. La dimension américaine devra donc être documentée pour être présentée comme un fait acquis. Une nomination dans une dynamique de développement mondial La nomination de Dominique Delafosse prend place dans cette ambition de développement international. Elle ouvre une nouvelle étape de représentation au sein d’une organisation qui entend associer ingénierie financière, partenariats et compétences opérationnelles au service de projets structurants. Pour Binti Invest, l’enjeu sera de traduire cette ambition en réalisations mesurables: des projets financés, des partenariats exécutés et des actifs durablement exploités. C’est sur cette capacité à transformer la complémentarité de ses métiers en résultats concrets que se jouera la portée de son développement international. items.description: Lundi 5 octobre 2026 Journee mondiale des enseignants : la situation du personnel enseignant au cœur des echanges La Journee mondiale des enseignants a ete celebree ce lundi 5 octobre. Cette journee est notamment consacree aux droits, aux responsabilites et aux conditions de travail du personnel enseignant. a Niamey, une ceremonie a ete organisee a cette occasion. Soumeila Zabeirou, secretaire general du Syndicat independant des cadres auxiliaires du ministere de l'education nationale, est revenu sur la situation des enseignants au Niger au micro de Hassane Nourou Abdourahamane. Le CCR examine la campagne agricole et l'approvisionnement en produits petroliers Une session extraordinaire du Conseil consultatif de la refondation, CCR, convoquee par le president de la Republique, a debute lundi a l'hemicycle. Pendant deux jours, les conseillers doivent notamment examiner la campagne agricole 2026, les stocks de cereales, la disponibilite des intrants agricoles ainsi que l'approvisionnement et la distribution des produits petroliers. Dr Mamoudou Harouna Djingarey, president du CCR, s'est exprime sur la necessite de securiser l'approvisionnement du Niger en produits petroliers, au micro d'Ali Nialli. Mardi 6 octobre 2026 Prix Dan Gourmou : les preparatifs de la 13ᵉ edition se poursuivent a Tahoua a Tahoua, les preparatifs de la 13ᵉ edition du Concours national de musique moderne du Niger, Prix Dan Gourmou, se poursuivent. L'evenement est prevu du 24 au 29 octobre. Cette manifestation culturelle vise notamment a faire vivre la memoire et l'œuvre de Dan Gourmou, presente comme une figure de la musique traditionnelle nigerienne. Habsatou Assoumane Abouba, representante de l'artiste, s'est exprimee sur les preparatifs au micro d'Ibrahim Badage. Penurie de carburant : de longues files d'attente observees a Niamey Depuis plusieurs jours, plusieurs centres urbains du pays, dont Niamey, connaissent une penurie de carburant. Dans la capitale, de longues files d'attente sont observees devant certaines stations-service. Selon plusieurs usagers interroges par Assoumana China, cette situation perturbe leurs activites quotidiennes. Mercredi 7 octobre 2026 Niamey : plusieurs innovations presentees au Salon africain de l'invention et de l'entreprise innovante Le Salon africain de l'invention et de l'entreprise innovante s'est tenu a Niamey du 5 au 7 octobre. Plusieurs innovations ont ete presentees dans differents domaines, notamment le numerique, l'alimentaire ainsi que des activites liees aux savoir-faire traditionnels. Alheri Harouna et Simone Illiassou ont visite plusieurs stands et recueilli les temoignages d'exposants. CCR : des recommandations sur la securite alimentaire, le pastoralisme et le carburant a l'issue de sa session extraordinaire tenue les 5 et 6 octobre, le Conseil consultatif de la refondation, CCR, a formule plusieurs recommandations sur les principaux sujets examines. Les conseillers ont notamment insiste sur la prevention des crises alimentaires, la securisation des espaces pastoraux et la diversification des sources d'approvisionnement en carburant. Les details avec Rahilatou Soumana. Jeudi 8 octobre 2026 N'Gourti : l'insuffisance des pluies entraîne une rarefaction des pâturages Dans le departement de N'Gourti, region de Diffa, l'insuffisance des pluies a entraîne une rarefaction des pâturages. Selon Adam Mohamed, representant des eleveurs, cette situation conduit un nombre croissant de pasteurs a se deplacer a la recherche de pâturages pour leurs animaux. Il a presente la situation au micro de Guidi Abdourahaman. Un projet d'insertion professionnelle des jeunes diplomes lance a Niamey Un projet consacre a l'insertion professionnelle des jeunes diplomes a ete lance jeudi matin a Niamey a l'initiative des autorites nigeriennes. Selon les responsables du projet, cette initiative vise a favoriser l'acces des jeunes diplomes a l'emploi et a contribuer au renforcement de la souverainete economique du pays. Ide Oumarou Abdou, directeur general de l'Agence nationale pour la promotion de l'emploi, ANPE, a apporte des precisions au micro de Hamidou Hama. Vendredi 9 octobre 2026 Octobre rose : des femmes se rendent dans les centres de sante pour le depistage du cancer du sein Dans le cadre d'Octobre rose, campagne de sensibilisation a la lutte contre le cancer du sein, des femmes se rendent dans des centres de sante de Niamey pour se faire depister. Cette demarche leur permet de connaître leur etat de sante et de beneficier d'un depistage. La reporter Simone Illiassou s'est rendue dans un centre de sante de la capitale pour recueillir les temoignages de plusieurs femmes. Matameye : des demarches pour faciliter l'acces des enseignants au carburant Dans un contexte de penurie de carburant signalee dans certaines villes, le bureau local du SYNACEB de Matameye, dans le departement de Kantche, a entrepris des demarches afin de faciliter l'approvisionnement en carburant des enseignants. L'objectif annonce est de permettre aux enseignants disposant d'un moyen de deplacement de rejoindre leurs postes dans de meilleures conditions en cette periode de rentree scolaire. Abdou Moussa Idi, secretaire general du bureau local du syndicat, a presente les dispositions prises au micro de Habou Sarki Saley.

items.title: Djokovic crashes out of Shanghai Masters in his first match
items.description: Novak Djokovic went down in straight sets to Hubert Hurkacz on Friday, exiting the Shanghai Masters in his first match after memorably winning the China Open this week. Big-serving Hurkacz, the 2023 champion in Shanghai, won 6-4, 6-3 as the 39-year-old former world number one faltered against an opponent a decade his junior. “I didn’t feel myself on the court,” the Serbian veteran said afterwards. “It’s a super-quick surface, completely different from Beijing. If you lose your serve, it’s enough to lose a match.” Djokovic was playing three days after winning the title in Beijing, where he has still never lost a match on the professional Tour. He hunched over and squatted down between points on a cool evening in Shanghai while a lively Hurkacz refused to give much away. Djokovic was broken in the fourth game of the second set as he double-faulted to give Hurkacz a 3-1 lead. The Pole held his serve to see out the win and will face either Italy’s Lorenzo Musetti or Chinese wildcard Zhou Yi in the third round. “It’s very difficult to return his serve, almost impossible,” Djokovic said of his opponent, who sent down 13 aces across the one-hour-and-28-minute match. “I didn’t adjust, and it was a really tough draw for me to play him in the first match-up.” Hurkacz had advanced to the Beijing semi-finals but ended his match early due to a strained muscle. It was his first-ever victory against Djokovic in nine meetings on the Tour. “It was a challenging match, always,” Hurkacz said. “I was pleased with how I performed, how I received in important moments.” – Zverev survives scare – Earlier, top seed Alexander Zverev churned out a win over Chinese wildcard Wu Yibing 6-4, 7-6 (7/4), and will next play Quentin Halys of France. A dive left the German world number two grimacing and grabbing his left ankle during the 11th game of the second set, with Wu, ranked 113th, going 6-5 up. But the 29-year-old held serve and forced a tie-break, capitalising on a series of errors to win on his second match point when the home hope fired long. “Credit to him, he was playing amazing tennis,” Zverev told the crowd afterwards. “He hits every ball as hard as he can.” Zverev is on track to end the year at number one after Jannik Sinner announced he was ending his season due to injury. – Birthday joy for Shelton – A gritty Ben Shelton beat Germany’s Daniel Altmaier 6-3, 7-6 (8/6) and will play France’s Arthur Gea in the third round. It was a fitting present for the American third seed, who turned 24 on Friday, though he hinted he may go easy on the celebrations, telling an on-court interviewer: “I hate cake.” Frenchman Adrian Mannarino upset sixth-seeded Flavio Cobolli 6-1, 4-6, 6-3 to set up a tie against Karen Khachanov. And Japanese qualifier Rei Sakamoto beat Russia’s Andrey Rublev 6-4, 6-4 to earn a match against ninth-seeded Alex de Minaur. The post Djokovic crashes out of Shanghai Masters in his first match appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Toilettes scolaires : des élèves obligés de se retenir faute d’hygiène
items.description: La rentree scolaire est effective depuis quelques jours a travers le pays. Mais dans de nombreux etablissements, l'etat des toilettes reste preoccupant. Manque d'hygiene, insuffisance d'entretien et mauvaises odeurs : certains eleves preferent eviter ces espaces, voire se retenir pendant les heures de cours. Face a cette situation, la question de l'entretien et des moyens disponibles se pose. a Mopti, Fatoumata Konipo, eleve, alerte sur les risques sanitaires lies a l'insalubrite des toilettes de son ecole. Elle plaide pour un entretien regulier afin de preserver la sante des eleves. « Nous, les filles, demandons a l'administration de chercher quelqu'un qui puisse entretenir les toilettes. Ce serait vraiment utile pour nous et cela nous eviterait certaines maladies » , explique-t-elle. a Bamako, le constat est similaire. Assetou Kone deplore egalement la salete des toilettes de son etablissement. Elle appelle ses camarades a prendre soin de ces espaces communs. « Dans notre etablissement, les toilettes sont sales » , regrette-t-elle. Le manque de moyens complique l'entretien Du cote des responsables d'etablissements, les difficultes d'entretien sont egalement reconnues. Le manque de moyens et de produits d'hygiene figure parmi les obstacles a une meilleure prise en charge des toilettes scolaires. a Yorosso, Moussa Goïta, directeur du premier cycle D, reconnaît que les toilettes de son etablissement sont en mauvais etat, notamment en raison du manque d'entretien. Selon lui, leur assainissement releve des eleves et du gardien de l'ecole. Au premier cycle B de Yorosso, Souleymane Kone juge l'etat des toilettes acceptable, tout en reconnaissant la necessite d'ameliorations. Il souligne toutefois les difficultes financieres auxquelles sa direction est confrontee. « Nos toilettes sont propres, mais elles ont toujours besoin d'amelioration. La direction n'a pas les moyens de s'en occuper a hauteur de souhait. Nous n'avons pas les produits d'hygiene necessaires, comme l'eau de Javel, le gresil et le savon » , explique-t-il. a Medina-Coura, le nettoyage est organise chaque semaine Certaines ecoles ont mis en place une organisation pour assurer l'entretien des toilettes. C'est le cas de l'ecole Mamadou-Diarra, a Medina-Coura, dans la capitale. Le nettoyage y est effectue chaque semaine. Selon Abdou Maïga, point focal de l'assainissement de l'etablissement, cette tâche est repartie entre les eleves des cinq cours du fondamental que compte l'ecole. Lors de notre passage, les toilettes etaient dans un etat juge acceptable. Une responsabilite partagee Pour Birama Daou, directeur de l'Academie d'enseignement de Diola, l'entretien des toilettes dans les etablissements du fondamental releve des comites de gestion scolaire et des directeurs d'ecoles. « Il est de leur responsabilite de mettre en place une organisation interne et de veiller a son bon fonctionnement » , precise-t-il. Malgre les initiatives prises dans certains etablissements, l'hygiene des toilettes reste une preoccupation pour de nombreux eleves. Dans les ecoles visitees, plusieurs affirment se retenir regulierement d'aller aux toilettes pendant les heures de cours, notamment a cause des mauvaises odeurs et du manque de proprete. Lire aussi : Les toilettes publiques "des endroits desagreables" selon les usagers L’article Toilettes scolaires : des élèves obligés de se retenir faute d’hygiène est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: Dakar sous le choc : le drame d’une vie volée (Par Matel BOCOUM)
items.description: Les Dakarois se sont réveillés sous les eaux en ce début de semaine. La plupart ont passé une journée cauchemardesque. De fortes pluies abattues sur Dakar ont pris en otage la capitale sénégalaise. Mais tous ont été bouleversés à l’annonce d’une autre tragédie : celle du décès de la dame Astou Pierre, après plusieurs mois d’hospitalisation. Elle venait de succomber à une grave agression à l’acide perpétrée par son ex-compagnon au mois de juin dernier sur son lieu de travail. Ce dernier a fini par mettre à exécution ses menaces avec une seule justification : « Tu es ma propriété ». Son décès a créé une onde de choc. Ce drame n’est que la face visible de l’iceberg et rappelle le cauchemar vécu au quotidien par de nombreuses femmes. Il révèle le degré de cynisme de certains hommes qui continuent de croire que les femmes leur sont assujetties, qu’elles ont été créées pour leurs beaux yeux ou leur plaisir. Ils s’arrogent librement le droit de semer le chaos dans la vie de celles qui ont eu le courage de les quitter ou de leur tourner le dos. Dans cette histoire, l’ex-compagnon d’Astou Pierre ne voulait pas accepter qu’elle puisse entretenir une relation avec un autre homme. Il lui a versé un produit corrosif au visage, lui causant des brûlures au troisième degré. Il a eu l’audace de mettre à exécution ses menaces. « Si tu ne m’épouses pas, tu ne seras la femme de personne ». Ce dossier remet sur le tapis la lancinante question des violences faites aux femmes, du féminicide et de la protection des victimes menacées. Beaucoup préfèrent subir sous le regard de la société et se résignent face aux supplices infligés par leur bourreau. Elles se rendent tardivement compte que les sacrifices faits au nom du bien-être de leur famille ne sont pas toujours proportionnels à leur investissement ni à leur don de soi. Dans son ouvrage intitulé « Femme africaine et luttes émancipatrices, de l’ombre à la lumière », l’auteur Donyo Koffi Agbenoko, maître de conférences en éthique, philosophie morale et politique, lève le voile sur une réalité : la hiérarchisation de la société qui a ancré, dans plusieurs sociétés, la domination de l’homme sur la femme. Malgré les efforts consentis par celle-ci pour rompre avec ces schémas, une réalité demeure tenace : des femmes sont encore dévalorisées dans certaines régions du monde. L’auteur met aussi en exergue une croyance ancestrale : la prétendue « faiblesse » des femmes africaines. D’aucuns le justifient par des arguments biologiques, physiques, psychologiques et intellectuels. Elles doivent continuer à jouer un rôle secondaire et se contenter de leurs fonctions de mère, d’épouse et de ménagère, qui ne doivent pas broncher. Pourtant, dans son ouvrage, comme dans plusieurs parutions d’auteurs africains, il est démontré que la femme s’est donné les moyens de s’affranchir de ce joug traditionaliste et qu’elle a su s’illustrer de manière admirable dans diverses luttes d’émancipation qui méritent une pleine reconnaissance. Seulement, leur situation appelle à une profonde réflexion. En effet, comme le souligne l’auteur, la structure sociale traditionnelle tend à maintenir les femmes dans l’ombre des hommes en les cantonnant à des rôles secondaires dans plusieurs sociétés. Le féminicide d’Astou Pierre montre les réalités de la condition féminine au Sénégal. Les organisations de femme ont beau tirer la sonnette d’alarme, il reste un acte mécanique et semble légitimer le harcèlement obsessionnel. Comme d’autres hommes, l’agresseur n’a pas supporté que cette initiative puisse provenir d’une femme. Comme lui, d’autres maintiennent cette doctrine de la propriété. « Tu resteras mienne ». Ils assimilent le corps des femmes à des biens matériels soumis au vouloir masculin. Lorsque la femme affirme son autonomie en mettant fin à la relation, elle peut s’attendre à des formes extrêmes allant du harcèlement moral à l’attentat physique. La mort d’Astou Pierre relance le débat sur la prise en charge des menaces de mort et le manque de dispositifs de protection effectifs pour les femmes en danger. Comme quoi, le poids de la tradition, la peur du « regard des autres » et la pression sociale incitent encore les victimes au silence ou à la résignation. matel.bocoum@lesoleil.sn

items.title: The One Question I Can’t Stand at Restaurants
items.description: A man walks into a restaurant. He doesn’t have a reservation, but that shouldn’t be a problem; there are ample seats at the bar, visible just over the hostess’s shoulder. “Of course,” she says, smiling. “We can seat you right away.” As she gathers menus, he absorbs the pleasant hum of a busy dining room, breathes in the tantalizing smells from the semi-open kitchen. Then, the hostess stops, Columbo-like, to interrupt with one more question: “And what’s your phone number?” The man was me. The restaurant was the Kingsway, a newish, Michelin-recommended spot in New Orleans. I’m not going to give you my phone number, but I gave it to the hostess, almost without thinking. And then, I did think about it: a lot. Throughout the meal, and for a long time afterward. There had been no reservation to check, no rewards program, no waiting list. So why the automatic ask? Let me say quickly that I liked the Kingsway very much. It’s coolly fancy, with a pan-Asian menu evoking the journey of the chef-owner Ashwin Vilkhu’s family from South Asia to the Gulf South. The result brings to mind an earlier era’s scruffy raiding of the global pantry, but this time executed with thought, technique, and precision. As I tucked into a tangle of Singapore-style chili-crab noodles, the term stoner soigné passed through my head. But that very first interaction with the hostess colored my meal. I brooded. What if I had just wanted to sit at the bar anonymously? Was that not one of life’s great pleasures? (I was working up a head of steam.) Was there no place in this enshittified world where a man could get a break ? [ Read: You will never get that restaurant reservation ] It mattered little that I knew the answer. Like pretty much everyone else, I am well aware that my information is strip-mined wherever I go, in more ways than I can count and in many that I will never know. Like everyone else, I spend my days downloading apps to operate things such as toothbrushes, unsubscribing from marketing lists by somehow giving up more personal information, rejecting cookies like I’m on a gluten-free diet. Nor am I overly romantic about restaurants, which I know have been collecting data for years. The reservation platform OpenTable began making algorithmic recommendations to users as early as 2014; by 2017, The New York Times reported that Big Data was “staging an intervention” to save the restaurant industry, which was suffering from stagnating growth and flattening profits. Much of the data collection has been justified in the name of customer service—a way to track allergies, preferences, birthdays, and so on, thus bringing technological efficiency to a job previously handled by a heavily notated reservation book or the encyclopedic mind of a gifted maître d’. “We try to build a database on everybody and get as much information as possible,” Vilkhu told me when I called him a few weeks after my dinner. His restaurant uses OpenTable, and he knew, for instance, which bartenders had served me, the friend who had joined me, that I had complimented the cocktail list and enjoyed the crawfish dumplings. This information, he assured me, was shared with the Kingsway’s sister restaurant but nobody else: “We just want to be able to curate the experience as best as we possibly can.” I believed him. But I was nevertheless a little shocked to go to the websites of the big reservation companies and see how they sold the impulse to care for guests to restaurants (which, in case it’s not clear, are their customers). At best, the sales pitches were dispiritingly cold, with talk of CRMs, GRMs, CDPs, and integrated tech stacks. At worst, they spoke of “capturing” guests’ data, “fostering loyalty,” and “upselling 24/7.” The “AI powered hospitality platform” Loyalist promised “a 360° view of every guest across dine-in and event spend,” itself a sentence seemingly powered by AI. The sales decks were like those optical illusions that turn from adorable to sinister when hit with different colored lights, flipping the language of care and hospitality to the language of surveillance and theft. Most striking was OpenTable’s promotion of a feature, currently in beta, called Global Insights. Until now, as Vilkhu had told me, whatever data a restaurant collected through the reservation platforms remained confined to that restaurant or restaurant group. Global Insights, which is available to OpenTable Pro subscribers, is the first feature to jump that garden wall and allow other restaurants access to the same information—in OpenTable’s words, to “get an idea of how your diners behave at other restaurants across the OpenTable Diner Network.” With an account, any restaurant can identify big spenders, diners who tend to linger at a table, diners who order a lot of drinks, frequent late-cancelers, and chronic “no-showers,” which I initially read as being about personal hygiene. [ Read: Please don’t make me download another app ] My outrage at this new invasion of privacy was accompanied by a pang of embarrassment: This is one of those times in history when it’s easy to get old fast, to wake up one morning and find yourself appalled by norms that everybody around you seems to take for granted. (For instance, the notion that one’s phone number remains a piece of intimate information.) Still, the idea of a restaurant I’d never been to using a dossier on me to decide, say, where I should sit, what I was likely to order, even whether I should be given a reservation at all, gave me chills. Curious to see what insights on me OpenTable might share with that hypothetical restaurant, I sent the company a request for my personal data. To its credit, the company makes this easy with an online form; less than 24 hours later, a zip file arrived. (Resy requires a request by email; a week later, I was told that it was “under review” and have heard nothing since. SevenRooms, another reservation platform, says that it is merely a processor of data and suggested that I contact individual restaurants.) The OpenTable file was 48 pages, in the monospaced typeface of computer code. Much of it was indecipherable, aside from dozens of instances of my phone number (aha!) and semi-redacted credit-card information. Despite its length, the document contained only a fraction of the reservations I’ve made over the years. The Kingsway wasn’t in there; neither was the first OpenTable reservation I can find in my records, at Zenkichi, a Japanese restaurant in Williamsburg that I visited in 2008. The file had a note that read “GIN,” which I grant was on the money about my inclinations, but it wrongly identified my home market as Austin. If this was truly the sum of OpenTable’s knowledge, I had less to immediately worry about than I’d anticipated. [ Read: Restaurants are the new factories ] At the same time, seeing the traces of past meals emerge from the sea of characters was eerie. Many I remembered; plenty I had not thought about since. Next to many of the restaurant names was appended a note: “Permanently Closed.” Lowlife, Church & State, Hunky Dory, La Mangeoire—all no more. Others didn’t have the tag, but I knew they were gone too. Like ghosts, they swam through the mists of the OpenTable servers, rattling chains forged of bad leases, unruly food costs, fickle trends, misbegotten dreams, and a thousand other maladies. I could almost hear them wail, “Doooooon’t judge ussss … We just wanted to stay aliiiiiive …” Indeed, restaurants are often asked to bear a moral and behavioral burden not generally placed on other small, low-margin, independent businesses. The more the public has learned about how restaurants work , the more they have scrutinized the ways in which they handle all sorts of social issues, such as racial and gender equity, climate change, and, yes, data privacy. These are all great and worthy considerations, but they do illustrate a gulf between how some customers (and many food writers) see restaurants and how many chefs and restaurateurs do: The former might like them to, you know, just solve the problem of ethical consumption under late-stage capitalism, while the latter are preoccupied with how to lower the cost of a lamb chop by 20 cents so they can pay that month’s electric bill. In the bigger picture, both diners and restaurateurs are reckoning with the same systemic forces. But the question remains. Knowing all of this—not to mention with a plate of crawfish dumplings before me—why was I so rankled that night when asked for my number? Maybe because it’s exhausting, these constant micro-negotiations between dignity and grift. Exhausting, and lonely: Most people know that completely opting out of data collection isn’t an option, short of walking into the woods. So we’re left to improvise which of the numberless small violations are worth summoning the energy to resist: when we’re willing to have an awkward interaction, how embarrassed our companion will be, which employee might get in trouble, whether making a scene is worth the hassle. Like so many things, we’re on our own. And maybe I am romantic about restaurants. About a 10-minute drive from the Kingsway is another restaurant, Crescent City Steakhouse, which opened in 1934. It features four booths along one wall that are outfitted with curtains that can be drawn for maximum privacy. A server once told the local paper that they were for “shady politicians, secret lovers, and people who put ketchup on their steaks.” I am none of those things, but I like to think I could be if I wanted. The idea that restaurants should be exempt from the pressures of modern society might be a fantasy, but I don’t think it’s an idle or shameful one. It is a large part of why people love restaurants, and, I have to assume, why people open them too. We want restaurants to be a respite from the world, or at least a plausible illusion of one. We want them to be the woods.

items.description: Barcelona captain Raphinha will miss the club’s next two matches after picking up a hamstring issue while playing for Brazil, coach Hansi Flick confirmed on Friday. “The picture shows something and it’s not a big injury,” Flick, who said that it nonetheless required attention, told reporters. “We have to take care about this because he has last season a lot of injuries about this. I think three injuries. “And we take care. So, he’s not available tomorrow (Saturday against Getafe in La Liga) and also not available in Istanbul against Galatasaray (on Tuesday in the Champions League).” The German manager was furious at the schedule imposed on the players which resulted in the Brazilian taking the knock during a friendly match in Australia. Repositioned as a centre-forward at Barcelona since the start of the season, Raphinha is the top scorer in Europe’s main leagues with 14 goals in eight matches across all competitions. But he has been plagued by recurring muscle problems throughout his career, returning injured from the March 2026 international break, during which he faced France in a friendly in Boston. The 29-year-old’s absence was sorely felt by Barcelona during the season’s final stretch, particularly in the Champions League when they fell in the quarter-finals to Atletico Madrid. The Brazilian forward also suffered a hamstring injury while playing for Brazil during the 2026 World Cup. The reigning two-time Spanish champions are unbeaten in La Liga this season and sit top of the table, five points ahead of Atletico Madrid. items.title: South Africa withdraws asylum directive after anti-migrant violence
items.description: South Africa’s Department of Home Affairs has withdrawn a directive allowing asylum applications following anti-migrant protests that turned violent in Johannesburg and Durban. The department announced the withdrawal on Friday, a day after protesters torched vehicles and looted foreign-owned shops in the two cities. The directive was intended to implement a July 7 Constitutional Court ruling that asylum seekers could not be denied access to the country’s asylum system solely on procedural grounds, including entering the country illegally. The department said the directive was introduced as an operational measure but overwhelmed refugee reception offices within days, putting officials at risk and threatening public safety and order. The government blamed the disinformation surrounding the court ruling, stressing that it did not automatically grant refugee status, permanent residence or other legal rights to undocumented migrants. South Africa, Africa’s largest economy, has experienced a surge in anti-immigrant protests, straining relations with other African countries and forcing thousands of foreign nationals to leave the country. Migrants are frequently blamed for unemployment, crime and pressure on public services, although social scientists say the allegations are unsupported by evidence. During Thursday’s violence, rioters set fire to 14 vehicles in Durban and 10 others in Johannesburg’s Soweto Township. Foreign-owned shops were also looted. A senior police official, Lt.-Gen. Puleng Dimpane, told a press briefing in Soweto that calm had returned to the area. Dimpane spoke near the remains of vehicles burnt during the violence. In Durban, police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda said the situation had stabilised, adding that a swift police response had prevented further damage. (Reuters/NAN) The post South Africa withdraws asylum directive after anti-migrant violence appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sondages en France : Glucksmann en tête des intentions de vote à la primaire de la gauche
items.description: Raphael Glucksmann, copresident de Place publique, apparaît comme le grand favori de la primaire dite « sociale-democrate » en France, dont le scrutin s'est ouvert ce 9 octobre. Selon un sondage Harris Interactive pour M6 et RTL, publie ce 9 octobre, cet eurodepute, connu pour evoquer quasi systematiquement Vladimir Poutine lors de ses prises de parole, est credite de 33 % des intentions de vote. « Je compte sur vous », a-t-il lance sur X, assurant vouloir « refonder la gauche democratique et la faire gagner en 2027 ». Loin derriere lui, Segolene Royal est creditee de 16 % des voix, soit sept points de plus que le premier secretaire du Parti socialiste, Olivier Faure, qui recueille 9 %. Quant aux deputes de l'Essonne Jerome Guedj et du Val-d'Oise Emmanuel Maurel, ils sont chacun credites de 5 %. Un ecart qui semble en adequation avec le ressenti des Francais se declarant de gauche et ayant suivi les debats : 28 % d'entre eux considerent Glucksmann comme « le plus convaincant », contre 14 % pour Segolene Royal, 12 % pour Emmanuel Maurel et Olivier Faure, et seulement 5 % pour Jerome Guedj. On notera au passage qu'Olivier Faure, dont le parti a su imposer son agenda au Premier ministre Sebastien Lecornu pour eviter la censure en janvier, n'a ete considere comme « le plus convaincant » que par 5 % des sondes a l'issue du debat du 24 septembre. Pour rappel, avant d'etre le conjoint de Lea Salame, presentatrice eploree par une partie de la presse francaise depuis son retrait du « 20 heures » de France 2, Raphael Glucksmann etait l'epoux d'Eka Zgouladze, ancienne vice-ministre de l'Interieur de Georgie, puis d'Ukraine. Il fut, entre 2009 et 2013, au lendemain de la guerre russo-georgienne, le conseiller du president georgien Mikheïl Saakachvili.

items.title: La Tunisie officielle se porte comme un charme
items.description: Les responsables du gouvernement ont la fâcheuse tendance de mettre la poussière sous le tapis et de brosser un tableau reluisant de la situation générale dans le pays. Zouhair Attallah, chef de cabinet du ministère des Finances, qui est parmi les mieux informés des indicateurs financiers de la Tunisie, ne déroge pas à cette règle. (Photo: ministère des Finances, La Kasbah, Tunis). Intervenant lors du 4 e Forum financier arabe du Prix de Sharjah pour les finances publiques, organisé à Tunis les 6 et 7 octobre 2026, en collaboration avec l’Organisation arabe pour le développement administratif (relevant de la Ligue des États arabes) et le Département central des finances de Sharjah, sous le thème «Résilience financière et durabilité : concevoir des budgets adaptables et maximiser la valeur pour l’argent public», il a déclaré que la Tunisie a réussi — malgré les crises sanitaires, les catastrophes naturelles et l'instabilité du contexte mondial — à faire preuve de résilience, à enregistrer des taux de croissance positifs et à maintenir l’inflation, le déficit et l’endettement à des niveaux qu’il a qualifiés d’ «acceptables» . «Ces résultats ont été obtenus grâce aux efforts considérables déployés par les institutions publiques et à une bonne préparation pour absorber et affronter ces circonstances exceptionnelles» , a-t-il précisé, selon le compte-rendu du forum diffusé sur la page Facebook du ministère, vendredi 9 octobre. M. Attallah a également souligné la démarche de réforme engagée par le ministère à court et moyen termes, notamment à travers le renforcement des cadres juridique, institutionnel, organisationnel et humain, la consolidation des principes de bonne gouvernance, ainsi que l’amélioration de l’efficacité et de la transparence des politiques publiques. Que de bonnes nouvelles en somme pour un auto-satisfécit que des économistes objectifs, examinant les indicateurs macroéconomiques de notre pays, trouveraient immérité. Avec une inflation de 5,3 %, un déficit budgétaire de 5,2 %, un endettement de 82 % et un chômage de 15,2 %, pour une croissance atone d’à peine 2,5 % (chiffres officiels de 2025), on ne peut pas dire que la Tunisie se porte bien ou qu'elle est en train d’avancer sur la voie du progrès socio-économique. Non seulement, notre pays a beaucoup régressé par rapport à ses indicateurs de 2010, mais il est en train de manger le pain de ses générations montantes en s’endettant à tour de bras. Et il ne s'endette pas pour investir dans la mise en place d’infrastructures publiques mais pour financer ses dépenses de fonctionnement, et notamment les salaires de ses 700 000 à 750 000 fonctionnaires, ni inventifs, ni productifs ni efficaces. Non, M. Atallah, la Tunisie ne se porte pas aussi bien que vous le dites ! Interrogez les Tunisiens, qui voient leur pouvoir d'achat régresser et leurs conditions de vie se détériorer jour après jour, ils vous diront exactement le contraire. I. B. L’article La Tunisie officielle se porte comme un charme est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: NNPC extends N66 petrol discount to October 31, denies subsidy return
items.description: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd) has extended its N66 per litre petrol discount across its retail outlets nationwide until October 31, insisting that the initiative does not amount to a restoration of petroleum subsidy. The company said the discount, initially introduced on October 1 to commemorate Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary, was intended to provide relief to motorists amid rising global crude oil prices linked to the conflict in the Middle East. In a statement issued on Friday, NNPC’s Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, said the company remained committed to supporting the Federal Government’s efforts to cushion the impact of rising fuel prices on households and businesses. The statement followed remarks by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, on October 8, 2026. NNPC said the initiative was designed to ease the burden of higher petrol prices on Nigerians, particularly the cost of transportation and business operations. “We recognise that higher petrol prices affect everyday life, from the cost of commuting to the expenses of running a business. We understand the strain on families and livelihoods, and this discount is intended to provide direct relief to customers during this difficult period,” the company said. It stressed, however, that the discount applied only to NNPC Retail outlets and did not establish a uniform national pump price or change the market-based pricing framework for petroleum products. “This discount is a customer relief initiative and does not represent the reintroduction of petroleum subsidy,” the statement said. The company urged Nigerians to disregard interpretations suggesting that the initiative marked a return to the petrol subsidy regime. NNPC added that it would continue to collaborate with the government and other stakeholders to ensure reliable product supply while providing practical relief to consumers. It also pledged to communicate the scope and duration of its customer initiatives clearly to enable Nigerians to make informed purchasing decisions. The statement, dated October 9, 2026, was posted on the X handle of the Special Adviser Information and Strategy to President Tinubu, Mr. Bayo Onanuga. The post NNPC extends N66 petrol discount to October 31, denies subsidy return appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sobowale’ Death: Nigeria has lost distinguished media scholar – Amosun
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Former Ogun State Governor, Senator Ibikunle Amosun, has described the death of renowned communication scholar, veteran journalist and former Lagos State Commissioner for Education, Professor Idowu Akanbi Sobowale, as a great loss to Nigeria’s media and academic communities and the nation at large. Amosun, in a condolence message said the late professor’s contributions to journalism, communication scholarship and education had left an enduring mark on the country. Sobowale, who died on Thursday at the age of 85, was widely recognised for his contributions to journalism practice, academic research and the professional development of communication studies in Nigeria. A veteran journalist, Sobowale had a distinguished career with Daily Times of Nigeria Limited, where he served as a war correspondent and assistant editor between 1964 and 1975. During his time at the newspaper, he contributed to the development of journalism in Nigeria, including the introduction of opinion polling into the country’s media practice. In academia, he distinguished himself as a teacher, researcher and professor of journalism, mentoring generations of students and scholars whose careers were shaped by his knowledge, guidance and commitment to scholarship. He also played a pioneering role in the Association of Communication Scholars and Professionals of Nigeria (ACSPN), serving as its chairman before becoming life chairman of its Board of Trustees. In these capacities, he contributed to advancing communication scholarship and strengthening professional standards within the discipline. Beyond journalism and academia, Sobowale served as Lagos State Commissioner for Education from 1999 to 2003, bringing his experience and expertise to public service. His contributions earned him the national honour of Officer of the Order of the Niger (OON), as well as the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 23rd edition of the Diamond Awards for Media Excellence (DAME). Reflecting on his personal relationship with the deceased, Amosun described Sobowale as a man of admirable character whose warmth and friendliness endeared him to those who knew him. “On a more personal note, I remember Prof. Idowu Sobowale as a man of noble character; friendly, accommodating and always pleasant to be with,” he said. “He exhibited these sterling qualities when our paths crossed in the late 1980s and early 1990s, when we were neighbours in the Gbagada area of Lagos State.” The former governor said Sobowale’s death was not only a loss to the media and academic communities, but also a personal loss to those who had the privilege of knowing him beyond his professional accomplishments. “His passing is therefore not only a loss to the media and academic communities, but also a personal loss to those of us who had the privilege of knowing him beyond his professional accomplishments,” Amosun added. Amosun extended his condolences to the Sobowale family, particularly the deceased’s wife and children, as well as his colleagues in the media and communication professions and others mourning his death. He prayed that Almighty God would grant the late professor eternal rest and give his family, friends, colleagues and associates the strength to bear the loss. The post Sobowale’ Death: Nigeria has lost distinguished media scholar – Amosun appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Azeri woman’s gang-rape case: Lahore court extends physical remand of two prime suspects by four days
items.description: LAHORE: A judicial magistrate extended on Friday the physical remand of two prime suspects by four days in an Azeri woman’s gang-rape case . The two prime suspects, arrested of the three accused in the case, were produced before Judicial Magistrate Azhar Mahmood at the Cantonment Courts following the expiry of their remand period. The case has been registered with Defence-C police on Sept 26 on the complaint of a 20-year-old Azeri woman, who had travelled to Pakistan for business purposes and was allegedly gang-raped by three men in a rented flat of a private housing society located near Raiwind. During the hearing on Friday, the investigating officer (IO) told the court that a substantial part of the investigation had been completed, but the police still needed to recover the suspects’ mobile phones. The IO sought an extension of their physical remand to recover their phones and complete the investigation. The magistrate accepted his request and extended the suspects’ remand by four days. The case Apart from the three prime suspects, the complainant has also accused two women of abetting the crime. One of them is on physical remand with the police while the other is on bail. On Sept 27, the complainant recorded her statement before Judicial Magistrate Muhammad Sagheer under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC). In her statement, she said she had arrived in Pakistan from Istanbul on Sept 13 and travelled to Lahore after staying in Faisalabad for five days. She said she had contacted two women to meet her in Lahore and later accompanied one of them to a house in Bahria Town, where she met the other. The group subsequently moved to an apartment, where three men allegedly raped her. The woman alleged that one of the men locked her in a room and the suspects refused to let her leave unless she drank alcohol with them. She said the men later threw her out of a car at an unknown location, threatened her against approaching the police and took her handbag containing Rs200,000 and two mobile phones. She also alleged that one of the women had taken Rs20,000 to Rs30,000 from a suspect, while both women were present during the events leading to the alleged assault. It is the second such case in which a foreign woman has been allegedly gang-raped in Lahore’s Defence-C police station area during the last four months. In June, two foreign women, nationals of the Netherlands and Venezuela, were allegedly abducted and sexually assaulted in the Defence-C police station area. According to the FIR, the women were abducted by five suspects, including a close relative of a senior political personality, who demanded ransom and subjected them to sexual assault during their captivity.

items.description: A survivor of domestic abuse, name withheld, has recounted how a marriage that began despite several warning signs descended into physical violence, threats to kill her, financial control, and emotional abuse. Ama, who shared her experience on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show during a discussion on why people remain in abusive relationships, said she decided to leave her marriage on her 25th birthday after realising that staying could cost her life. The moment she decided enough was enough When asked what finally made her decide to leave, Ama pointed to an incident in which she used a metal bar to defend herself during an attack. She said she had run from the hall into the bedroom and picked up a bar normally used to bolt the door when her husband rushed towards her. She used it to strike him in self-defence. However, she said he subsequently reported that she was the one physically abusing him. Ama said this accusation changed how she viewed the relationship because it showed her how easily her husband could reverse roles and present himself as the victim. “For a very long time, I’ve been suffering, I’ve been going through this, and the first time I stand up for myself, everything that he has been doing to me, he’s turned around and made me the aggressor,” she said. She described the incident as the beginning of her awakening, helping her recognise that what she was experiencing was neither normal nor an expression of love. “I started realising that any husband who actually loves his wife will not subject the wife to these types of things,” she said. “This is not love. This is not protection. This is not care.” Ama said she made the decision to leave on her 25th birthday. She separated from her husband and later completed the divorce process. She said she made the decision after spending considerable time weighing the consequences of leaving against the danger of staying in the marriage. She said the abuse began with emotional manipulation before escalating into physical violence shortly after the marriage. “Before the marriage itself, we did have a few issues. I did see a few red flags. But I was in love, and I believed that things would change with time,” she said. Ama said she went ahead with the marriage despite those concerns, hoping her partner’s behaviour would improve. However, she said the situation deteriorated rapidly after they married. “Before that, there was emotional abuse. But when we got married, the physical abuse actually started,” she said. According to her, her husband often took out his frustrations over problems with his business on her, sometimes reacting violently to seemingly minor issues. She recalled an incident in which he beat her because she had moved a television remote from the place where he normally kept it. “These little things were what was triggering him,” she said. Warning signs she mistook for love When asked about the warning signs she noticed before the marriage, Ama said her partner repeatedly questioned her choice of friends and tried to control important decisions in her life. She said he would insist that her friends were not good for her, regardless of whether they were male or female, and suggested that she should make him her closest friend instead. He also expected her to discuss important decisions, including the courses she wanted to take, with him before proceeding. Ama said he further discouraged her from turning to her family for support, insisting that he was now her family and that she should approach him first whenever she needed help. Looking back, she believes these behaviours were early attempts to isolate her from people who could have supported her when the abuse began. “At that age, I didn’t realise that he was gradually alienating me from people who would have been my support system at the time I was going through the abuse,” she said. When asked whether she had discussed the relationship with friends or family before getting married, Ama said she had kept the problems to herself because she believed she was in love. She said the couple had an understanding that problems within the relationship should not be discussed with outsiders. “There was this, I don’t know if I can call it a rule that we have in the relationship, that whatever issues we have stay in the relationship. We do not discuss our problems with outside people,” she said. Ama said she only understood much later that what she had interpreted as love was controlling behaviour that left her increasingly isolated. Church and families urged her to stay Ama said the abuse became so severe that she eventually began standing up for herself, talking back to her husband and fighting back when he attacked her. She also refused to continue having physical intimacy with him. Her husband subsequently reported her to their church, accusing her of failing to fulfil her duties as a wife. When asked whether people had tried to persuade her to remain in the marriage, Ama said the church intervened after she disclosed what was happening behind closed doors. She said her husband had presented a different version of events, portraying himself as the victim and suggesting that she was punishing him for not meeting her demands. However, when she explained the abuse she had suffered, church leaders realised how serious the situation had become. Despite this, she said they believed the marriage could be saved and encouraged the couple to attend counselling. The church also advised her husband to find better ways of expressing his anger, including leaving the house when he felt angry. Ama said both families were eventually brought into the discussions, but they also believed the marriage could be repaired. “They were of the view that it could be fixed and that I needed to amend my behaviour so that when he is angry, he would have no reason to take it out on me,” she said. She rejected that advice, saying that the problem was not her behaviour but her husband’s willingness to use violence whenever he wanted to vent his frustration. “I didn’t need to do anything necessary. And also, I was the one in the situation. I was the one feeling the fire,” she said. “Everybody else telling me to wait or telling me to fix it or telling me to stay were not the ones being subjected to the beating.” Ama said she eventually decided that she could no longer continue living in the marriage, regardless of the expectations of others. Financial control and repeated humiliation Beyond the physical violence, Ama said her husband controlled her access to money and prevented her from working. She explained that she married shortly after completing her national service and was not allowed to take up employment. As a result, she depended entirely on her husband for financial support and had to ask him whenever she needed money. She said there were times when he treated the money he gave her as an act of charity rather than a responsibility within the marriage. “There was a point he even said that was charity, that he was doing me a favour,” she said. Ama also described how her husband regularly insulted her, compared her with his former girlfriend and other men’s wives, and told her that nobody else would want to marry her. She said the verbal abuse was not limited to their home but also occurred in public. Recounting one incident during a journey, she said her husband became angry when she appeared to be falling asleep and began insulting her in front of other passengers. She said she was afraid to respond because doing so could make the situation worse. “He would even scream some more, saying that I am rude and that when my husband was talking, I’m talking back and all of that,” she said. Ama said the experience was humiliating, particularly because her husband had already created the impression that she was responsible for the problems in their marriage. She added that he also pressured her to attend family events and engage in physical intimacy, making her feel that refusing him meant she did not love him or was disgracing him. The cumulative effect of the abuse, she said, took a serious toll on her mental health. She was eventually diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and an anxiety disorder, which she attributed to her experiences during the marriage. Lasting eye damage after a beating One of the most serious incidents Ama recounted involved an attack that left her with a black eye and permanent damage to the nerves in one of her eyes. When asked whether the abuse had ever resulted in a hospital visit, she confirmed that she had suffered an injury that affected her vision. She said the damage had left her with distorted vision in one eye, a condition she would have to live with for the rest of her life. Ama said her husband apologised repeatedly before taking her to hospital and begged her not to tell medical staff what had really happened. Instead, she said, he instructed her to claim that she had fallen while sleeping and hit her head against a bedside table. “He made sure that that was what happened because when we got to the hospital, he insisted on being part of the consultation,” she said. Ama explained that her husband remained present during her treatment, leaving her afraid to disclose the truth. When asked why she had been so frightened of him, she said he had threatened to kill her on two occasions. She said she believed the threats because he repeatedly claimed that his family background and influence would protect him from the consequences of his actions. “He had threatened to kill me, not once but twice,” she said. “I was actually scared that it would happen.” Ama said these threats also contributed to her decision not to report the abuse to the police at the time. She feared that taking action could cost her life and doubted whether the authorities would be able to protect her, given her husband’s claims about his influential background. Locked outside naked for more than an hour Ama also recounted an incident in which her husband attacked her after becoming angry that she had been making plans to apply for jobs without telling him. She said she had started looking for work secretly because she was not allowed to work openly. After an argument, she said her husband began beating her, forcing her to run out of the house almost naked. She said he then locked her outside, leaving her standing in the compound for more than an hour. People nearby witnessed what had happened, she added. The incident was one of the few occasions when others had a clearer view of the abuse she was experiencing. Ama said neighbours had previously heard her shouting, particularly after she began fighting back, but they did not necessarily understand the circumstances behind the arguments. She recalled that one neighbour had tried to advise her, apparently believing that she was a nagging wife who needed to complain less. Ama said she did not explain what was happening and simply thanked the person for the advice. She believes her husband’s efforts to portray her as the source of their marital problems made it harder for people to recognise her as the victim. Therapy and support helped her recover Reflecting on life after the marriage, Ama said therapy had played an important role in helping her rebuild her confidence and mental strength. She also said reconnecting with supportive people had been essential to her recovery. “I was able to build back my mental strength and my self-esteem from my therapy sessions,” she said. “Another thing that has been useful is rebuilding my support system.” Ama said surrounding herself with people who encouraged her, rather than making her feel defined by her past, had helped her move forward. Her experience, she said, had taught her the importance of recognising unhealthy behaviour early and refusing to dismiss warning signs in the hope that a partner would change. ‘Be strategic about your exit plan’ When asked what advice she would give to people experiencing similar abuse, Ama urged those in relationships to take warning signs seriously rather than assuming that controlling or abusive behaviour would improve with time. “If you are in a relationship, you shouldn’t ignore the signs,” she said. She encouraged people to pay attention when a partner attempts to control their friendships, isolate them from family, dictate their decisions or make them feel worthless. For those who are married and considering leaving an abusive relationship, she advised them to plan carefully and seek appropriate legal support. “If you are married, you should also leave. But you should be very strategic about it,” she said. “Because if you make your plans known, you might probably not get out of it quickly or as a full human being, if I can put it that way.” She advised those planning to leave to get a lawyer and proceed with divorce where appropriate, while taking their personal safety into account. Ama acknowledged that divorce often carries social stigma, particularly in communities where people are pressured to preserve their marriages regardless of what happens behind closed doors. She believes this pressure can keep people in dangerous situations long after they have realised that the relationship is harming them. But she said fear of judgement should not prevent anyone from seeking safety and rebuilding their life. “Honestly, there’s life after divorce,” she said. “You will find yourself again. The things that you’ve been restricted to do, the friends and family that you don’t have access to, you can have all of that back.” For Ama, leaving was not simply the end of a marriage. It was a decision to reclaim her safety, independence, and future after years of abuse. “You just need to get out of that situation first, and then you’ll be fine.”

items.title: N100m damages against SERAP: Appeal Court fixes Oct 13 for hearing
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri The Court of Appeal in Abuja on Friday deferred until October 13 the hearing of two separate appeals seeking to nullify a judgment that ordered the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) to pay N100 million in damages for defaming two officials of the Department of State Services (DSS). The two appeals, marked CA/ABJ/CV/1114/2026 and CA/ABJ/CV/1105/2026, were filed by SERAP and its Deputy Director, Mr. Kolawole Oluwadare, respectively. Although a three-member panel of the appellate court, led by Justice Danlami Senchi, initially heard the first appeal and reserved judgment, the entire proceedings were voided after it was discovered that the second appeal, which arose from the same set of facts, was not ripe for hearing. The appellate court took the decision after counsel to the second appellant, Ms. Hannah Ayanwale, drew its attention to the fact that her client’s brief had been served on the respondents only before the sitting commenced. Stressing that the two appeals ought to be heard together, the panel vacated the proceedings that led to the reservation of the first matter for judgment. It ordered the respondents to file their brief of argument by October 12, while the appellants were directed to file a response before the adjourned date. A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) sitting at Maitama had, in a judgment delivered on May 5 by Justice Yusuf Halilu, said it was satisfied that the non-governmental organisation had, on September 9, 2024, tarnished the reputations of two DSS personnel, Sarah John and Gabriel Ogundele, when it falsely alleged that they invaded its office in Abuja. The court held that SERAP, sued alongside its Deputy Director, Mr. Oluwadare, unjustly defamed the operatives when it published on its website and X (formerly Twitter) handle that they invaded the office and harassed a staff member. According to the court, the publication was in bad taste. Consequently, in addition to the N100m damages, the court ordered SERAP to tender public apologies to the defamed DSS operatives in two national newspapers, on two television stations, and on its website. Furthermore, it ordered the defendants to pay the two operatives N1m to cover the cost of the litigation, as well as 10 percent annual interest on the judgment sum until it is fully liquidated. The judgment followed Suit No. CV/4547/2024, which the two operatives filed before the court to challenge what they regarded as SERAP’s false claim, which had negatively affected both their reputations and the corporate image of the DSS. The second appellant, Oluwadare, had clarified the organisation’s work and the events surrounding the alleged invasion of its Abuja office by DSS operatives in his testimony before the trial court. Answering questions under cross-examination, Oluwadare told the court that DSS operatives had stormed the organisation’s office, a development that prompted it to alert the public. He added that several SERAP staff members, including a front-desk officer, a security guard, and a lawyer, had reported the officials’ presence. Asked if the staff members were assaulted or if doors were broken, the witness confirmed there was no physical attack. He insisted, however, that the manner of entry and the presence of unmarked vehicles used by the operatives had led SERAP to issue a public statement. Oluwadare further stated that the organisation has CCTV footage of the incident, adding that messages SERAP sent out through its X handle reflected the seriousness of what its staff members observed that day. Dismissing suggestions that the organisation exists only to criticise the government, he insisted that SERAP’s mandate is to promote and protect human rights, including socio-economic rights, in the overall public interest. He maintained that the harassment and intimidation of civic actors pose a grave threat to SERAP’s work and hamper its efforts to hold public institutions accountable. The appellants are praying the court to set aside the High Court judgment in its entirety, insisting that the trial judge erred in law and occasioned a miscarriage of justice against them. The post N100m damages against SERAP: Appeal Court fixes Oct 13 for hearing appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Benue Attack: Four-year-old, two others killed in Otukpo
items.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi A four-year-old boy and two others have been killed in an attack by suspected armed herdsmen on Omulonye community in Ugboju District of Otukpo Local Government Area of Benue State. Several other residents reportedly sustained injuries in the attack, which forced residents to flee their homes and seek refuge in neighbouring communities. Sources in the area said the attackers invaded the community at about 9pm, shooting sporadically and triggering panic among residents. One of the sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, described the attack as unprovoked, saying it lasted less than an hour. “It was an unprovoked attack. The people were in their homes, preparing to go to bed, when they started hearing gunshots, triggering pandemonium. People tried to escape, but three persons were killed instantly,” the source said. The source identified one of the victims as a four-year-old boy whose mother was badly injured. The boy’s uncle was also among those killed. “Many others sustained injuries. Most of those who sustained injuries were rushed to the Federal University of Health Sciences Teaching Hospital in Otukpo for immediate medical attention,” the source added. The source said the victims had been buried, while surviving residents had fled their ancestral homes and taken refuge in neighbouring communities. “As we speak, the residents have fled their ancestral homes and are taking refuge in neighbouring communities, while many others are said to be stranded,” the source said. When contacted, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, confirmed the attack and the death toll. “Yes, the reports are true. Three persons were confirmed dead in the attack, and efforts are being made to identify and arrest the perpetrators,” he said. The post Benue Attack: Four-year-old, two others killed in Otukpo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Côte d’Ivoire : une dizaine d’influenceurs poursuivis dans une affaire d’escroquerie et de blanchiment
items.description: Une affaire d'escroquerie presumee impliquant plusieurs figures des reseaux sociaux secoue la Cote d'Ivoire. Le Pole penal economique et financier a engage des poursuites contre une dizaine d'influenceurs, notamment pour association de malfaiteurs et blanchiment de capitaux, selon les informations communiquees par la justice. Au centre du dossier figure Rita Djedje, accusee d'avoir organise la vente de parcelles de terrain dont elle n'etait pas proprietaire. Selon le procureur national financier, Jean-Claude Aboya, une soixantaine de personnes ont porte plainte contre elle, estimant avoir ete lesees dans le cadre d'operations realisees par l'intermediaire de la societe Ivoire Challenge Corporation. Le prejudice total est evalue a pres de 320 millions de francs CFA, soit environ 547 000 dollars. D'apres les elements presentes par le parquet, l'influenceuse aurait percu frauduleusement cette somme avec l'aide d'autres personnalites du web. Des temoignages diffuses sur les reseaux sociaux denoncent egalement les methodes de promotion employees pour convaincre les acheteurs. Certaines videos attribuees a Rita Djedje mettent notamment en scene des promesses de cession de terrains, dont une sequence dans laquelle elle annonce a une femme qu'elle lui offrira une parcelle. Plusieurs personnalites du web visees Les poursuites concernent egalement des personnalites qui s'etaient affichees aux cotes de Rita Djedje pour lui apporter leur soutien. Parmi elles figurent l'influenceur Apoutchou National, deja condamne pour blanchiment de capitaux quatre mois auparavant, l'ancien footballeur international Geoffroy Serey Die et Pantcho Le Gatair. Certains des influenceurs cites ont publie des videos pour se desolidariser de Rita Djedje. Les poursuites engagees a leur encontre s'inscrivent dans le cadre plus large de l'enquete judiciaire sur cette affaire. Le procureur a, par ailleurs, requis un mandat de depot contre Rita Djedje. Cette requisition ne constitue pas, a elle seule, une decision definitive de placement en detention. La Cote d'Ivoire sous surveillance du Gafi Au-dela des personnes mises en cause, cette affaire intervient alors que la Cote d'Ivoire cherche a renforcer sa lutte contre le blanchiment de capitaux et les circuits financiers illicites. Le pays figure depuis deux ans sur la liste grise du Groupe d'action financiere (Gafi), qui recense les juridictions soumises a une surveillance renforcee en raison de lacunes dans leurs dispositifs de lutte contre le blanchiment d'argent et le financement du terrorisme. Les autorites ivoiriennes esperent toutefois obtenir une sortie de cette liste lors de la pleniere d'octobre 2026, apres les progres annonces dans la mise en œuvre du plan d'action convenu avec le GAFI.

items.title: What happens to Nigerians living in communities without NNPC stations? – Atiku’s aide faults 30-day petrol discount
items.description: Paul Ibe, media adviser to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, has criticised the Federal Government’s 30-day petrol price reduction initiative, arguing that it would not provide adequate relief to Nigerians because of the limited reach of NNPC retail outlets. Ibe, who disclosed this in a post on his X handle on Friday, said the government should prioritise making petrol affordable nationwide rather than engaging in arguments over whether the price reduction amounted to a subsidy or a discount. “Nigerians need relief, not semantics,” he said, accusing the President Bola Tinubu administration of focusing more on terminology than on addressing the economic hardship faced by citizens. While welcoming any genuine reduction in petrol prices, Ibe insisted that the relief must be fair, accessible and sustainable. He argued that the limited geographical spread of Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) retail outlets would prevent many Nigerians from benefiting from the initiative. According to him, Nigeria has approximately 22,681 filling stations, while NNPC operates more than 900 outlets, representing about four per cent of the nationwide retail network. He added that NNPC’s estimated retail market share stood at 17 per cent in 2024, while the company’s July 2026 report showed petrol availability across its retail network at 52 per cent. Ibe questioned how the government intended to deliver meaningful nationwide relief through a network with limited coverage and documented supply challenges. “How does the government propose to provide meaningful nationwide relief through a network with such limited geographical coverage and documented supply challenges?” he asked. He also questioned what would happen to Nigerians living in communities without NNPC stations, arguing that they might have to travel long distances and incur additional expenses to benefit from the discount. The former vice-president’s aide warned that the arrangement could create unequal access to affordable petrol, drawing a comparison with the electricity Band A, B and C classification, under which consumers face different service conditions depending on their locations and tariff categories. “Petrol affordability must not become another postcode lottery,” he said. Ibe maintained that, regardless of whether NNPC forfeited its retail margin or the government directly subsidised consumers, the initiative amounted to an acknowledgement that market forces alone could not shield Nigerians from high petrol prices. He argued that the administration was attempting to address a nationwide affordability crisis through a retail network representing only a small fraction of the country’s filling stations. “Nigerians deserve more than a 30-day experiment,” he said. Ibe advocated Atiku’s proposed production-based subsidy, which he said would reduce costs at the point of production and allow the benefits to flow through the wider distribution network. He argued that such an approach would offer a more sustainable way to make petrol affordable across the country. “You cannot solve a nationwide affordability crisis with a narrowly targeted discount. Nigerians need cheaper petrol everywhere, not cheaper petrol somewhere, and certainly not for just 30 days,” he said. Ibe further accused the Tinubu administration of moving back towards what he described as an opaque subsidy regime, despite its earlier position that the petrol subsidy had been removed.
